papers.title: A Reproducible Pre-Transplant γδ T-cell Effector Signature Reveals Immune-Metabolic Programs Associated with Kidney Allograft Rejection
papers.authors: Kim, S. M.; Sur, S.; Koser, K.; Pineda, S.; Bestard, O.; Koyama, T.; Hoffmann, T.; Sigdel, T. K.; Sirota, M.; Babdor, J.; Spitzer, M. H.; Sarwal, M. M.
papers.abstract: Despite optimized immunosuppression, acute kidney transplant rejection affects 10-20% of recipients within the first year, and no reliable pre-transplant molecular test exists to identify patients at high risk, independent of the donor HLA matching. Across three independent cohorts of kidney transplant recipients, profiled by bulk RNA-sequencing with T-cell receptor repertoire analysis, flow cytometry, CyTOF with paired metabolomics, we identified a reproducible depletion of {gamma}{delta} T cells associated with rejection: an elevated {beta}/{gamma}{delta} T cell ratio in two post-transplant, biopsy-matched cohorts, and depletion of specific {gamma}{delta} T effector clusters in a third, longitudinally sampled cohort. In this third cohort, {gamma}{delta} T cell depletion was already present at the pre-transplant baseline in patients who subsequently developed rejection and remained detectable across the transplant course, indicating that it reflects recipient baseline immune biology rather than a consequence of graft injury. Longitudinal metabolomic profiling in this cohort identified time-dependent metabolic changes, including in amino acid metabolism that co-occur with the {gamma}{delta} signature and converge with it upon multi-omics integration. At the pre-transplant baseline, {gamma}{delta} T-cell marker expression alone showed exploratory discriminatory value for rejection risk (AUC = 0.69), improving marginally when integrated with metabolomic features (AUC = 0.71); larger prospective studies will be needed before clinical translation.

papers.title: LOTUS: lineage-aware optimal transport reconstructs continuous clonal fate dynamics
papers.authors: Lu, J.; Hou, H.; Zhang, Z.; Lin, Y.; Lin, Y.; Zhou, P.
papers.abstract: Destructive sampling in single-cell sequencing obscures ancestor-descendant relationships, limiting the continuous reconstruction of cell-fate dynamics. Here we present Lineage-aware optimal transport for unbalanced single-cell dynamics (LOTUS), a framework that integrates time-resolved transcriptomic snapshots with clonal lineage information from engineered barcodes or endogenous T cell receptor clonotypes. LOTUS couples clone-level optimal transport with neural unbalanced transport to model continuous cellular state change, population growth and clonal propagation under lineage-consistent constraints. In branching simulations, LOTUS reduced lineage-inconsistent transport relative to benchmark methods, lowering off-target routing from 4.94-14.84% to 1.10%. On LARRY lineage-barcode scRNA-seq of hematopoiesis, LOTUS reconstructed branching trajectories, improved early neutrophil-monocyte fate-boundary prediction, and inferred multi-fate progenitors and fate-biased meta-clones, linking their distinct fate potentials to inferred epigenetic priming. On CellTagging scRNA-seq of fibroblast reprogramming, it distinguished reprogrammed from failed trajectories and prioritized fate-associated perturbation genes. In longitudinal scRNA-seq and TCR-seq of malaria-responsive memory (CD45RA-) CD4+ T cells, it preserved endogenous clonotype structure and reconstructed TR1 dynamics and regulatory networks. LOTUS thus converts lineage-resolved single-cell snapshots into interpretable, continuous models of fate dynamics and their regulatory programs.

papers.title: Inherited maternal memory T cells protect offspring from respiratory viral infection through disease tolerance
papers.authors: Toure, H.; Jimena, B.; Caban, M. E.; Lederer, E. E.; Rico, D. M.; Medlin McFadden, A.; Abideen, S.; Kokati, P.; Harrington, W. E.; Koch, M. A.
papers.abstract: Maternal immune transfer is a powerful mechanism for early-life protection from infection, yet the full repertoire of protective factors remains unknown. We discovered that maternal memory T cells are both necessary and sufficient to protect offspring from lethal respiratory infection. This antigen-specific protection operated independently of maternal antibodies and offspring T cell responses and required IL-10 produced by maternal T cells. Transfer of protective maternal T cells reduced offspring inflammatory responses and lung tissue damage without affecting viral burdens, indicating that maternal memory T cells directly suppress pathogenic innate inflammatory responses to preserve offspring health. Critically, maternal vaccination similarly protected offspring in a T cell-dependent manner. These findings reveal maternal antigen-specific T cell transfer as a complementary immunological defense mechanism to protect offspring against pathogens that escape maternal antibodies, with broad implications for maternal vaccination strategies.

papers.title: irAEGIS: Pathway-guided interpretable prediction of immune-related adverse events
papers.authors: Budhkar, A.; Guo, S.; Zhang, X.; Su, J.; Song, Q.
papers.abstract: Immune-related adverse events (irAEs) are major complications of immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy and remain difficult to predict prior to treatment initiation. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) provides a unique opportunity to characterize immune states associated with future irAE development. However, translating single-cell measurements into accurate and biologically interpretable patient-level risk predictions remains challenging. Existing approaches typically aggregate cellular profiles into patient-level summaries, thereby obscuring cell type specific signals, or rely on complex deep-learning architectures that offer limited insight into the biological pathways and mechanisms underlying their predictions. Here, we present irAEGIS, a pathway-guided interpretable model for predicting irAE risk from pre-treatment scRNA-seq data. irAEGIS incorporates prior biological knowledge through gene set constrained representation learning, aggregates pathway activities within individual cell types, and integrates cell type specific risk signals through a hierarchical prediction framework. This design enables predictions to be decomposed into contributions from individual cell types, pathways, and genes, providing interpretable explanations across multiple biological resolutions. Across simulated datasets and independent pre-treatment ICI cohorts, irAEGIS consistently outperformed seven existing methods. Beyond predictive performance, irAEGIS identified biologically coherent immune programs associated with irAE risk. In non-small cell lung cancer, irAEGIS highlighted neutrophil-associated inflammatory pathways linked to future irAE development, whereas in melanoma, it identified apoptotic and immune activation pathways in CD8+ NKT-like cells associated with severe irAEs. These findings were independently supported by pathway enrichment, cell-cell communication, and trajectory analyses. Together, irAEGIS provides a biologically informed and interpretable model for linking single-cell immune states to patient outcomes, enabling both accurate risk prediction and mechanistic insight into immune-related adverse events. More broadly, irAEGIS establishes a general strategy for interpretable phenotype prediction and biological discovery from single-cell transcriptomic data.

papers.title: Cellular origin and characterization of autoantibodies against type I IFNs in COVID-19 and APS-1.
papers.authors: Sun R, Lin S, Simonelli L, Strunz B, Behere A, Pedotti M, Xu T, Zuo F, Du L, Wan H, Lestani S, de Campos-Mata L, Vlachiotis S, Kalmár D, Karolinska KI/K COVID-19 Study Group, Strålin K, Aleman S, Ljunggren HG, Piralla A, Baldanti F, Kämpe O, Bensing S, Hammarström L, Landegren N, Zeng Z, Björkström NK, Varani L, Marcotte H, Pan-Hammarström Q.
papers.abstract: Autoantibodies against type I IFNs can severely compromise antiviral defense, yet the mechanisms underlying their development remain elusive. Using high-throughput autoantigen profiling, we observed that a subgroup of severe COVID-19 patients exhibited strong binding to multiple type I IFNs. Integrated single-cell RNA and B cell receptor (BCR) sequencing with functional analysis identified B cell subsets/states enriched for IFN-α2-binding and -neutralizing antibodies in COVID-19. These findings were compared with those from patients with autoimmune polyendocrine syndrome type I, a rare genetic disease characterized by defective immune tolerance and persistent type I IFN autoimmunity. Competition surface plasmon resonance and AlphaFold 3 structural modeling identified three major functional epitope groups and seven predicted structural subclasses among neutralizing antibodies. Our results indicate that IFN-α2 autoreactivity is present in both naive and antigen-experienced B cell compartments, whereas functional IFN-neutralizing antibodies are predominantly associated with memory and atypical B cells, consistent with defective tolerance and affinity maturation-mediated selection of autoreactive B cell clones.

papers.title: Integrative bioinformatics and experimental validation of the prognostic and functional relevance of XDH and ITPA in non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.authors: Zhang W, Song J, Zhu H, Wang Y, Wang H, Li X.
papers.abstract: Purine metabolism has been implicated in tumor biology and immune regulation, but the clinical and biological relevance of purine metabolism-related genes in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains incompletely defined. Transcriptomic data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and the Genotype-Tissue Expression (GTEx) project, together with TCGA clinical data, were analyzed to identify differentially expressed purine metabolism-related genes and assess their prognostic associations. Immune infiltration was evaluated using single-sample gene set enrichment analysis (ssGSEA), and single-cell transcriptomic datasets were analyzed to characterize the cellular context of candidate genes. Stemness features and drug sensitivity were assessed using transcriptome-based computational models. XDH and ITPA protein expression was examined by Western blotting and immunohistochemistry (IHC) in an independent NSCLC cohort and in cell models. Stable knockdown of XDH or ITPA was performed in H1299 cells, with key functional findings further evaluated in A549 cells. Cisplatin sensitivity was assessed using cell-viability dose-response assays in H1299 and A549 cells. Several purine metabolism-related genes were upregulated in NSCLC and associated with overall survival (OS). XDH and ITPA showed higher protein expression in tumor tissues and were associated with adverse clinicopathological features and poorer survival. Higher expression of these genes was also associated with altered immune infiltration patterns. The messenger RNA-based stemness index (mRNAsi) was associated with ITPA and XDH expression in different directions, whereas higher XDH expression was associated with higher predicted half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) values for cisplatin. Knockdown of XDH or ITPA attenuated proliferative, clonogenic, migratory, and invasive phenotypes in H1299 cells, with key findings reproduced in A549 cells. XDH knockdown also reduced the experimentally determined cisplatin IC50 in both H1299 and A549 cells. XDH and ITPA may represent candidate prognostic and functionally relevant purine metabolism-related genes in NSCLC. The integrated clinical, computational, and cellular findings support their association with NSCLC progression-related phenotypes, while the underlying molecular mechanisms and broader clinical applicability require further investigation.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics of pediatric tuberculosis lymph nodes reveals a conserved hypoxia_SPP1 niche
papers.authors: Adebiyi, S. O.; Goussard, P.; De Wet, D. R.; Janson, J. T.; Jooste, T.; Shabangu, A.; Dorhoi, A.; Bondoc, S.; Nekorchuk, M.; Chao, M. C.; Fortune, S. M.; Busman-Sahay, K.; Estes, J. D.; Shamskhou, E. A.; Urdahl, K. B.; Gerner, M. Y.; Walzl, G.; Du Plessis, N.
papers.abstract: Pediatric tuberculosis (TB) often presents as primary disease involving the mediastinal lymph nodes; however, its granuloma microenvironment remains poorly characterized because these population patient tissues are rarely available for study. Here, we use spatial transcriptomics to profile 60 granulomas from four children aged 4 to 36 months. We identified nine recurrent transcriptional microenvironments shared across granulomas, despite their marked histological heterogeneity. One macrophage-rich microenvironment showed strong hypoxia-associated activity and secreted phosphoprotein 1 (SPP1) enrichment. This microenvironment was present in both non-necrotic and necrotic lesions and overlapped with a Mtb-persistence macrophage signature previously identified in murine TB lymph nodes. Pathway analysis revealed the enrichment of both antimicrobial and regulatory programs within this microenvironment, suggesting partial immune control rather than uniform inflammatory or suppressive activity in this region. SPP1 expression was associated with regions enriched for both M1- and M2-like macrophages, suggesting a macrophage program that extends beyond conventional polarization classifications and may be influenced by the local granuloma microenvironment. We further observed a similar spatial association between hypoxia-associated activity and SPP1 expression in an independent adult TB dataset (pooled Spearman {rho}=0.65) and validated this association at protein level by multiplex immunofluorescence in our pediatric TB granuloma sample. Overall, this study identified a hypoxia-associated SPP1-enriched microenvironment that may contribute to incomplete bacterial clearance and could provide a framework for evaluating host-directed strategies to enhance sterilizing immunity without exacerbating tissue damage.

papers.title: Extracellular DDR1 targeting remodels collagen-rich tumor stroma and local immunity
papers.authors: Huang, X.; Liu, X.; Huang, L.; Jing, G.; Kuerban, K.; Cai, M.; Yue, Q.; Yu, M.; Yang, S.; Zhu, Y. Z.; Ye, L.
papers.abstract: Collagen rich stroma can restrict immune cell access and sustain immune exclusion in solid tumors, but strategies that directly target extracellular matrix organizing receptors remain limited. Here, we develop cross reactive nanobody Fc proteins against extracellular discoidin domain receptor 1 (DDR1) and identify DDR1nb 3 Fc as a lead molecule with activity in immunocompetent mammary and pancreatic tumor models, including an orthotopic pancreatic model. Tumor control is accompanied by altered collagen architecture and remodeling of the intratumoral immune compartment rather than consistent direct tumor-cell growth inhibition. Single cell profiling with mouse level compositional and pseudobulk analyses reveals reproducible pathway level remodeling of tumor associated neutrophils, while Ly6G positive cell depletion significantly modifies the antitumor effect of DDR1nb 3 Fc. These findings identify extracellular DDR1 as an actionable regulator of collagen rich tumor stroma and support its targeting as a strategy to reshape the tumor microenvironment and promote tumor control.

papers.title: CTLA-4 checkpoint signalling modulates germinal centre dynamics and antibody avidity during Borrelia burgdorferi infection in mice.
papers.authors: Mäkinen, V. J.; Alinikula, J.; Fair-Mäkelä, R.; Sundqvist, P.; Salmi, M.; Mattila, P.; Pietikäinen, A.; Hytönen, J.
papers.abstract: Borrelia burgdorferi, the causative agent of Lyme borreliosis, persists in mammalian hosts despite robust activation of innate and adaptive immunity. A hallmark of murine infection is the production of low-avidity antibodies, yet the immunological mechanisms underlying this defective humoral response remain poorly understood. Here, we used single-cell RNA sequencing of draining lymph node cells from Borrelia-infected mice at days 7 and 14 post-infection, comparing transcriptional profiles with those from mice immunised with heat-killed Borrelia or with a potent germinal centre-inducing protein immunisation. Borrelia infection induced a rapid germinal centre response, however, light zone B cells displayed diminished expression of co-stimulatory and T-B cell interaction molecules while maintaining core germinal centre identity markers, suggesting impaired positive selection. T follicular helper cells upregulated multiple inhibitory checkpoint receptor genes, most prominently Ctla4, alongside an active germinal centre engagement programme. Foxp3? regulatory T cells upregulated genes associated with follicular-homing and suppressive function, including those implicated in CTLA-4-mediated trans-endocytosis. To test whether inhibitory signalling contributes to the impaired humoral response, infected mice were treated with anti-CTLA-4 blocking antibody. CTLA-4 blockade significantly increased plasma cell numbers and enhanced both the magnitude and avidity of Borrelia-specific IgG responses, including the induction of complement-fixing IgG2a. These findings reveal that CTLA-4-dependent inhibitory signalling contributes to defective antibody quality during Borrelia infection, identifying a mechanism by which dysregulated T cell responses may facilitate impaired humoral control of a persistent spirochaetal pathogen.

papers.title: FedEpitope: Parameter-Efficient Federated Protein Language Models for Linear B-Cell Epitope Prediction
papers.authors: Joshi, D.; Priyadarsinee, L.; Chatterjee, B.; Natarajan, A. M.; Sastry, G. N.
papers.abstract: Linear B-cell epitopes are antigenic regions recognised by antibodies that play crucial roles in vaccine development, antibody production, and other therapeutic applications.Their prediction can support peptide-based vaccine candidate screening and diagnostic assay development, but the experimental data required for model development may be distributed across institutions that cannot freely pool their records. We present FedEpitope, a federated framework that adapts the ESM-2 protein language model for peptide-level linear B-cell epitope prediction using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), keeping client-partitioned data local and restricting the communicated trainable model state to approximately 1.11 MB. Simulated benchmarks of FedAvg and FedProx algorithms, evaluated using homology-aware data splits of five biologically heterogeneous, organism-partitioned clients, achieve promising global test performance without centralising training data, with FedAvg outperforming all single-client models in mean AP, F1, and MCC. Additional experiments characterise post-federation personalisation, record-level differential privacy, sensitivity to controlled client heterogeneity, LoRA rank, and generalisation to the independent BCPreds and NetBCE benchmarks, demonstrating the feasibility of parameter-efficient federated protein language model adaptation for data-localised B-cell epitope prediction and the associated trade-offs among predictive performance, personalisation, privacy, communication efficiency, and distribution shift.

papers.title: Aging reshapes cardiac extravascular leukocyte transcription through bidirectional remodeling during LPS-induced endotoxemia
papers.authors: Yu, Q.; Gao, H.; Fang, F.; Du, J.; Wang, M.
papers.abstract: Sepsis disproportionately affects older adults and is frequently complicated by cardiac dysfunction. However, how aging alters the transcriptional responses of cardiac extravascular immune cells during systemic inflammation remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated aging-dependent transcriptional remodeling of cardiac immune cells using an LPS-induced endotoxemia model in young and aged C57BL/6 mice. Mice received intraperitoneal LPS (5 mg/kg body weight) or vehicle, and cardiac extravascular leukocytes were isolated from ex vivo retrogradely perfused hearts 24 h later for single-cell RNA sequencing. Aging was associated with bidirectional transcriptional remodeling, characterized by both up- and downregulation of gene programs, particularly in cardiac macrophages, monocyte-like macrophages, T cells, and B cells following LPS challenge. A shared feature across these four cell populations was reduced representation of mitochondrial-associated transcriptional programs, indicating aging-dependent remodeling of mitochondrial biology across cardiac myeloid and lymphoid lineages during systemic inflammation. In parallel, cell type-specific transcriptional remodeling revealed distinct functional-associated responses. Macrophages and monocyte-like macrophages exhibited increased tissue-remodeling and repair-associated transcriptional programs. Both T and B cells showed reduced metabolic programs but increased actin cytoskeleton organization. T cells additionally exhibited reduced cytotoxicity-associated and enhanced Th17-associated transcriptional programs, whereas B cells showed reduced antigen-processing and presentation programs. Cell-cell communication analysis suggested aging-associated differences in immune cell interactions following LPS challenge and potential features of cardiac inflammaging at baseline. Together, these findings demonstrate that aging bidirectionally reshapes the cardiac immune response to systemic inflammation, characterized by shared remodeling of mitochondrial-associated programs and cell type-specific changes in inflammatory, metabolic, cytoskeletal, and effector-associated programs. These aging-dependent transcriptional changes occurred in the context of the greater severity of illness observed in aged mice following LPS-induced endotoxemia.

papers.title: Comprehensive prospective investigation of splicing variants in the coding region of RHD: Insights into phenotypic consequences including revision of RHD*weak D type 3.
papers.authors: Fichou Y, Tournamille C, Thomas G, Plaire C, Barrault A, Marec N, Pochard P, Bénech C, Floch A.
papers.abstract: As splicing has been shown to be commonly altered by single nucleotide variants (SNVs) in the RHD gene, resulting in a mild to severe drop in the expression of the D antigen, we sought to identify prospectively those deleterious SNVs that may disrupt splicing. All potential substitutions affecting the coding deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) sequence (CDS) of the RHD gene were scored by using two in silico tools: SpliceAI and SPiP. In the 25 top-score SNVs selected for functional analysis, 11 variants either partially (N = 8) or completely (3) disrupted splicing, suggesting that the quantitative expression of the D antigen may be negatively affected. Interestingly, the c.8C>G variant defining the RHD weak D type 3 allele was found to impair splicing dramatically both in vitro and in vivo, while the p.(Ser3Cys) amino acid substitution in the RhD protein is not responsible for the decrease in the membrane expression of the D antigen. Overall, our fundamental findings redefine the functional effect of the RHD weak D type 3 allele and emphasize the complex regulation of D antigen expression. This prospective work also illustrates how the combination of computational and experimental analyses is instrumental for rare variant interpretation and genotype-phenotype correlation studies.

papers.title: A single-cell comprehensive atlas of leukemia and its microenvironment.
papers.authors: Wang B, Kuo YA, Dasdemir E, Xiao W, Rebboah E, Tang G, Wang W, Abbas HA.
papers.abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) remains highly lethal, with treatment failure and relapse driven by dynamic cellular states and evolving interactions within the leukemic ecosystem. In this study, we built a comprehensive atlas of leukemia and its microenvironment (CALM) by integrating single-cell profiling from 73 AML samples and 9 healthy donors, bulk RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) from 87 newly diagnosed patients, and 4 paired bone marrow and peripheral blood single-cell data. All datasets were linked to clinical, cytogenetic, molecular, and treatment-response annotations. Immune analysis revealed diverse T cell distribution across disease status, where patients with persistent disease exhibited greater clonal expansion. Machine learning modeling on conventional T cells identified a T-cell signature pertinent to AML and outcomes, which were validated in two cohorts. CALM is a publicly accessible and interactive portal (calm.mdanderson.org) for exploring cellular compartments, cell-cell interactions, and longitudinal transcriptional and clonal dynamics to enable hypothesis generation, biomarker discovery, and target validation.

papers.title: Sequencing and analysis of the human adaptive immune receptor repertoire.
papers.authors: ElAbd H, Franke A.
papers.abstract: Adaptive immune cell populations (T cells and B cells) retain a molecular record of immune exposures, including infection and vaccination, in their specific antigen receptor repertoires. These receptor repertoires arise through V(D)J recombination, which assembles distinct combinations of germline-encoded V, D and J gene segments and introduces extensive junctional diversification to generate highly diverse antigen receptors that are subsequently shaped by developmental selection and antigen exposure. Recent advances in high-throughput sequencing enable adaptive immune receptor repertoires to be profiled at scale, across large cohorts and with increasing depth within individual samples. As a result, receptor repertoire profiling is emerging as a powerful approach for monitoring disease course and treatment responses in cancer, quantifying immune responses to infection and vaccination, and dissecting the immunological basis of inflammatory disease. In this Review, we discuss how human T cell and B cell receptor repertoires are formed, how inherited genetic variation shapes their architecture and how experimental and computational advances are enabling repertoire data to be translated into biological insight, clinical utility and repertoire-guided therapeutic opportunities.

papers.title: Integrative single cell and machine learning analysis identifies fibroblast centric hub genes and therapeutic candidates in lung adenocarcinoma and ischemic cardiomyopathy.
papers.authors: Pu Z, Liu Z, Zhang H, Han Y.
papers.abstract: Background Ischemic cardiomyopathy (ICM) and lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) are distinct diseases but may share fibroblast mediated mechanisms involving tissue remodeling and inflammation. However, their common molecular features at single cell resolution remain insufficiently defined. Methods We integrated single cell RNA sequencing datasets from ICM and LUAD with bulk transcriptomic profiles from TCGA LUAD, GSE18842, and GSE48166. Differential expression analysis identified 36 shared core genes. A total of 127 combinations of machine learning algorithms and feature selection methods were benchmarked to identify six hub genes: KRTCAP3, RUNX2, DBF4B, C11orf80, COL3A1, and ZFP64. UCell, scMetabolism, SCISSOR, Monocle 3, CellChat, scTenifoldNet/scTenifoldKnk, virtual drug screening, and molecular docking were used for functional characterization. Results Fibroblasts were the dominant cellular source of the six hub genes in both ICM and LUAD. COL3A1 progressively increased along fibroblast pseudotime trajectories. Virtual overexpression and knockout analyses showed convergence on extracellular matrix organization, inflammatory response, and immune regulation. Cell communication analysis identified fibroblasts as major senders of COLLAGEN signaling, with recipient cells shifting from inflammatory monocytes under normal conditions to proliferating macrophages in ICM and tumor cells in LUAD. Molecular docking nominated Digoxin, Ergotamine, and Ledipasvir as candidate RUNX2-binding compounds with favorable predicted docking scores. Conclusions This study provides a single cell framework linking ICM and LUAD through fibroblast driven extracellular matrix remodeling and inflammation, and identifies potential molecular targets and therapeutic candidates for further validation.

papers.title: The TCR Motif Atlas: a database of specificities for TCRs recognizing viral, cancer, and autoimmune epitopes.
papers.authors: Tadros DM, Shah A, Roessner RA, Racle J, Gfeller D.
papers.abstract: T-cell recognition is elicited by the binding between T-cell receptors (TCRs) and epitopes. Many machine learning approaches have been proposed to model TCR-epitope recognition specificity, but most of them act as black boxes. To visualize TCR-epitope recognition specificity, we developed the TCR Motif Atlas (https://tcrmotifatlas.unil.ch). This database builds upon the probabilistic framework of TCR specificity profiles (TSPs) to visualize V and J genes as well as complementarity-determining Region 3 (CDR3) lengths and amino acids enriched in epitope-specific TCRs with respect to baseline TCR repertoires for hundreds of epitopes. An interactive interface enables users to build TSPs based on their own set of TCR sequences to investigate epitope recognition specificity or to explore potential biases in TCR repertoires of known or undetermined specificity. The TCR Motif Atlas further provides links to curated compilations of epitope-specific TCRs and crystal structures of TCR-epitope complexes.

papers.title: Clonal hematopoiesis and cytopenias following CAR19 therapy.
papers.authors: Hamilton MP, Phillips N, Noordenbos T, Boegeholz J, Sugio T, Sworder BJ, Alig SK, Good Z, Schroers-Martin JG, Tamaresis J, Esfahani MS, Lu Y, Olsen M, Liu CL, Ehlinger Z, Desai M, Muffly L, Negrin RS, Arai S, Johnston L, Lowsky R, Meyer E, Rezvani A, Shizuru J, Weng WK, Shiraz P, Sidana S, Bharadwaj S, Smith M, Dahiya S, Sahaf B, Frank MJ, Mackall CL, Diehn M, Kurtz DM, Miklos DB, Alizadeh AA.
papers.abstract: CD19-directed chimeric antigen receptor T cell therapy (CAR19) improves survival in relapsed/refractory large B cell lymphoma compared with immunochemotherapy with intent for autologous hematopoietic cell transplantation (autoHCT). However, major toxicities include prolonged cytopenias, infection and secondary hematologic malignancies. Here, to investigate these complications, we studied patients with lymphoma receiving CAR19 and compared clinical outcomes to propensity-matched autoHCT-treated controls. CAR19-treated patients exhibited impaired immune reconstitution and increased infection. Bone marrow analysis showed that prolonged post-CAR cytopenias are associated with clonal cytopenias of undetermined significance and interferon-mediated inflammation. Clonal hematopoiesis (CH) commonly expanded following CAR19 infusion and was associated with impaired immune reconstitution and treatment-related myeloid malignancy (tMN). Post-CAR tMN was molecularly and clinically comparable to post-autoHCT tMN. Single-cell DNA analysis revealed mostly independent CH clones, while CAR integration into CH-mutant T cells occurred frequently and may drive expansion and persistence. Together, these findings implicate CH expansion and marrow inflammation in key CAR19-associated toxicities.

papers.title: Self-reported health history from 70,724 individuals reveals novel HLA associations with allergy and other frequently underreported conditions.
papers.authors: Boquett JA, Yu-Tseng Lin S, House JS, Ahn KK, Burkholder AB, Suseno R, BakenRa A, Guthrie K, Wright M, Motsinger-Reif AA, Maiers M, Hollenbach JA.
papers.abstract: Background Variation in the HLA loci, located on human chromosome 6p, has been associated with hundreds of diseases and conditions. However, high levels of polymorphism that characterize the HLA system, coupled with generally modest effect sizes for most phenotypes, necessitate relatively large sample sizes to power association studies; meanwhile, high resolution HLA genotyping remains relatively resource intensive. These constraints limit identification of novel associations. While phenome-wide association studies (PheWAS) in the context of large registries with available electronic health records (EHR) have revealed new insights into the role of HLA in disease, many common health conditions are poorly represented in EHR due to the temporal nature of their occurrence or general underreporting. Further, these studies have generally been conducted with HLA genotyping data imputed from microarrays, rather than direct measurement of high-resolution genotypes. Objective To overcome these limitations and reveal novel HLA associations we undertook a PheWAS in many previously understudied health conditions. Methods We queried over 290 conditions, diseases and traits from 70,724 subjects registered with NMDP (formerly known as the National Marrow Donor Program) with available high-resolution HLA genotyping (HLA-A, HLA-B, HLA-C, HLA-DRB1, and HLA-DQB1). After stratifying according to self-reported geographic ancestry, we performed a logistic regression analysis adjusting for sex and age for HLA-phenotype association. Results We identified 48 significant HLA associations across self-reported geographic ancestry groups, confirming several known associations and uncovered fourteen novel associations. Most novel associations pertained to common infectious or allergic phenotypes that often go under-reported in the EHR. We identified a previously underappreciated yet very strong association between HLA-DRB1*04:01 and self-reported cefaclor adverse-reaction label of unverified mechanism (OR = 3.74, p-value 5.10E-28), which remained highly significant after excluding individuals reporting multiple drug hypersensitivities (OR = 3.13, p-value = 5.60E-15). Exploratory computational co-folding structure-and-affinity prediction identified a potential interaction between cefaclor and the P4 pocket of HLA-DRB1*04:01, providing a hypothesis-generating structural rationale that requires functional validation. If validated in independent cohorts with clinically characterized phenotypes and functional studies, this association may inform pharmacogenomic risk stratification and targeted prevention of adverse drug reactions. Other novel associations found, such as susceptibility to genital warts (HPV) and allergic rhinitis, reveal new insights into the role of specific HLA alleles in immune-mediated disease. Many of these novel associations were replicated in the independent All of Us cohort (AoU), while others showed the same trend for association, confirming the validity of this approach. Conclusion Collectively, our findings demonstrate the value of integrating population-scale, high-resolution HLA genotypes with phenotyping beyond the EHR to reveal immunogenetic influences on common health outcomes. These findings motivate future functional studies and validation in clinically characterized cohorts to refine mechanistic understanding and determine potential clinical utility.
papers.venue: The Journal of allergy and clinical immunology

papers.title: Activating death receptor 5 exposes a cancer cell vulnerability to natural killer and T cell attack.
papers.authors: Chen Z, Raffi GC, Zhao Z, Yang C, Chen J, Feng X, Chen Y, Steur M, Morandi P, Lieftink C, Lu S, Xie H, Zhong H, Wang J, Willemsen L, Horlings H, Beijersbergen R, Dijkstra KK, Gao S, Xue R, Bernards R, Wang L.
papers.abstract: Immunotherapy has revolutionized cancer care, yet resistance frequently undermines its efficacy. Although tumor-intrinsic resistance pathways have been mapped, how immune pressure regulates death-receptor vulnerability and anti-apoptotic buffering remains less defined. Using genome-wide CRISPR-Cas9 screening in cancer cells co-cultured with natural killer (NK) cells, we identify CFLAR, encoding cFLIP, as a dominant suppressor of death-receptor signaling that impairs NK- and T-cell cytotoxicity. CFLAR depletion sensitizes cancer cells to NK- and T-cell attack in vitro and in vivo. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analyses link high CFLAR expression to reduced lymphocyte infiltration and poorer responses to immune checkpoint blockade. Mechanistically, immune effector cell-induced inflammation increases CFLAR and death receptor 5 (DR5) expression in association with p38-MAPK signaling, balancing survival and death under immune pressure. The DR5 agonist conatumumab enhances lymphocyte-mediated killing and improves responses to cellular therapies, checkpoint blockade, and chemo-immunotherapy. Combining DR5 agonism with NKG2A blockade co-activates NK- and T-cell responses and overcomes anti-PD-1 resistance in MHC-I-deficient tumors. These findings identify the DR5-cFLIP axis as an immune-pressure-associated, pharmacologically targetable vulnerability and support rational combinations of DR5 agonists with multiple immunotherapies for refractory cancers.

papers.title: Macrophage Contribution to Tumour Matrisome in Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
papers.authors: Suwal U, Siljamäki E, Nissinen L, Rappu P, Riihilä P, Kähäri VM, Heino J.
papers.abstract: To investigate the direct contribution of macrophages to the tumour matrisome in human cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (CSCC), we established a three-dimensional spheroid-based coculture model incorporating CSCC cells, fibroblasts, and macrophages derived from the THP-1 cell line. This model also enabled comparison between interleukin-4-induced (M2-like) and interferon-γ-induced (M1-like) macrophages. RNA sequencing revealed differential expression of matrisome-associated genes, including the pro-tumorigenic chemokines CXCL6, CCL18, and CCL13, which were associated with M2-like macrophages, whereas CXCL9 was associated with the M1-like phenotype. NanoString analysis of CSCC tumours and normal skin confirmed increased expression of these chemokines in CSCC. The spheroid model also demonstrated substantial macrophage plasticity, particularly among initially M1-like macrophages. Mass-spectrometry-based proteomics identified galectin-9 (LGALS9) as the most prominently increased core-matrisome protein in spheroids. Immunohistochemical analysis of clinical samples confirmed significantly greater galectin-9 accumulation in CSCC metastases than in non-metastatic primary tumours. Analysis of publicly available single-cell RNA-sequencing data showed that LGALS9 expression was associated with CD86 high macrophages and further supported the macrophage origin of the identified chemokines. High LGALS9 expression correlated with reduced numbers of CD8 + T lymphocytes and increased expression of the galectin-9 receptor HAVCR2 (TIM-3) and T-cell exhaustion markers in CD8 + cells. Collectively, these findings suggest that galectin-9 may suppress CD8 + T-cell responses and contribute to an immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment. High galectin-9 expression may therefore serve as a marker of altered immune regulation in CSCC, particularly in metastatic disease.

papers.title: Knockdown of the long isoform of the prolactin receptor selectively targets pathogenic immune cells in systemic lupus erythematosus and averts glomerular pathology.
papers.authors: Rodrigues Lima-Junior J, Hu Z, Hamane K, Kumar A, Taghi Khani A, Sanchez Ortiz A, Guo X, Jung DH, Qin H, Tao S, Sanz I, Meffre E, Marzan K, Koff JL, Lorenson MY, Gu Z, Wu X, Walker AM, Swaminathan S.
papers.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is an autoimmune disease characterized by chronic inflammation in multiple organ systems. Although elevated circulating levels of the hormone/cytokine prolactin (PRL) have long been associated with increased SLE activity, the extent to which different isoforms of the prolactin receptor (PRLR) contribute to disease pathogenesis has not been explored. Here, we show that immune cells in SLE have aberrant splicing of the PRLR such that the ratio of the long (LF) to short (SF) splice isoforms is increased. To determine whether change in PRLR isoform expression was causal in this disease, we used a splice-modulating oligomer that knocks down expression of the LFPRLR while increasing expression of the SFPRLRs. Using patient samples ex vivo, SLE-prone mice in vivo, high-dimensional flow cytometry, and single-cell RNA sequencing, we demonstrated that the aberrant PRLR isoform expression in SLE both directly and indirectly contributes to the generation of autoreactive immune cell phenotypes. Accordingly, LFPRLR knockdown (KD) reduced STAT1 phosphorylation, decreased expression of type I interferon signaling/response genes known to be biomarkers and hub genes for SLE, reduced immunoglobulins with autoreactivity-associated sequence features, and averted glomerular pathology in SLE-prone mice. Importantly, LFPRLR KD reduced pathogenic B cell and other immune subsets that drive B cell activation, without negative impact on healthy donor counterparts. Current treatments for SLE adversely affect healthy cells and do not concurrently eradicate multiple pathogenic immune subsets. As LFPRLR splice-modulating oligomer does not share these disadvantages, KD of the LFPRLR represents a potential treatment strategy for SLE that merits further investigation. The long prolactin receptor (LFPRLR) represents an attractive therapeutic target in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Upper left: individuals with SLE exhibit aberrant increases in their relative transcript expression of the counteractive long (LF) to short (SF) PRLR isoforms. The aberrant increase in the ratio of LF:SF in SLE contributes to increased phosphorylation of STATs, predominantly STAT1. Upper right: aberrant increase in relative expression of LF:SF contributes to autoreactive immunophenotypes and glomerular pathology. Bottom: an SMO, which specifically prevents synthesis of only the LFPRLR and can increase expression of the counteractive SFs, tilts the balance of PRLR splice isoforms in favor of the SFs and reduces pathogenic signaling, immunophenotypes, and glomerular damage in SLE. Exons and introns are not drawn to scale. GC, germinal center; IFN-I, type I interferons; NK, natural killer; TLR, Toll-like receptor.

papers.title: Autoimmune-shared immune states converge in a CXCL12-CXCR4 fibroblast-immune niche in chronic antibody-mediated rejection.
papers.authors: Xia X, Bai Y, Yang B, Mao W, Yang H, Li Y, He Y, Wu J, Cai B, Fan Y, Yu H, Guo Y, Liu Y, Tang X, Yan H, Zhou T, Deng Y, Wu W, Cao M, Shu Y, Shi YY, Xu H, Wang L.
papers.abstract: Chronic antibody-mediated rejection (CAMR) is a leading cause of late kidney allograft failure and shares features of chronic immune activation with systemic autoimmune diseases, but how circulating immune states connect to spatially organized graft injury and whether related immune features recur in autoimmune inflammation remain unclear. Here, we integrated single-cell profiles from peripheral blood and kidney graft samples from patients with CAMR or stable allograft function and healthy controls with independent transplant cohorts, bulk transcriptomic datasets, spectral flow cytometry, multiplex immunofluorescence, high-resolution spatial transcriptomics, and a large blood immune reference spanning autoimmune and inflammatory diseases. CAMR was associated with reproducible myeloid expansion and enrichment of SLC8A1 + monocytes/macrophages, ANK3 + CD4 + memory T cells, ZEB2 hi T cells, and CD16 + NK cells. These subsets showed migratory and tissue-interacting transcriptional features, including recurrent CXCR4 and ZEB2 expression, suggesting candidate immune states potentially linked to local graft immune organization. In graft tissue, CXCL12-expressing fibroblasts and CXCR4-expressing immune cells were increased in CAMR. High-resolution spatial transcriptomics localized this fibroblast-immune architecture to perivascular regions marked by endothelial activation and stromal remodeling and placed CAMR-associated immune states within adjacent immune-rich neighborhoods, supporting a CXCL12-CXCR4 axis that may be associated with local immune accumulation. Comparisons with large-scale blood immune reference data and spatial transcriptomic datasets from rheumatoid arthritis and systemic lupus erythematosus suggested partial recurrence of related immune states and fibroblast-immune organization. Together, this study links circulating CAMR immune remodeling to a spatially organized CXCL12-CXCR4 fibroblast-immune niche and suggests that elements of this niche recur across alloimmune and autoimmune inflammation.

papers.title: Borrelia burgdorferi binds serum amyloid A and modulates subcutaneous adipose tissue immune signaling.
papers.authors: Esterly AT, Du S, Lee B, Johnson E, Odell A, Sefik E, Yu Q, Cui Y, Ayyala H, Haykal S, Odell I, Flavell R, Fikrig E, Zapata HJ.
papers.abstract: Following a tick bite, Borrelia burgdorferi spirochetes replicate in human skin and disseminate through tissues, including subcutaneous adipose tissue. Adipose is a complex organ containing both immune and non-immune cells that play a significant role in the immune response, yet little is known about adipose-specific immune signaling after B. burgdorferi infection. We investigated the landscape of immune signaling within adipose tissue-resident cells during B. burgdorferi infection in human tissue (skin and adipose tissue) ex vivo . Single-cell sequencing pathway analysis revealed upregulation of inflammatory pathways in skin, yet overall downregulation of immune pathways in adipose tissue cells during B. burgdorferi infection. Adipose-resident myeloid cells and adipose stem/progenitor cells (ASPCs) displayed an inflammatory profile characterized by the increased expression of IL-1β, TNF, and NFKB1. CellChat, a cellular communication comparative analysis, showed increased cell-to-cell communication across adipose-resident cell populations. ASPCs demonstrated the strongest outgoing signals, positioning them as key hubs of intercellular communication in adipose tissue. Interestingly, we observed adipose-specific downregulation of serum amyloid A (SAA), an inflammatory serum marker known to have antimicrobial properties and typically elevated in Lyme disease patients during acute infection. Therefore, we further evaluated the interaction between SAA and B. burgdorferi . Here, we show that human recombinant SAA protein directly binds B. burgdorferi spirochetes, reduces spirochete viability in a dose-dependent manner in vitro, and enhances phagocytosis. Taken together, these findings show that adipose tissue is a site of active immune signaling in the setting of infection and identify SAA as a host defense factor against B. burgdorferi .IMPORTANCE Borrelia burgdorferi is the bacterium that is transmitted by ticks and causes Lyme disease. These bacteria replicate in the skin to cause the localized skin rash erythema migrans, then disseminate to cause symptoms in other organs, including the joints and heart. Adipose tissue, or fat, is adjacent to skin, joints, and heart-all target organs of infection. In this study, we set out to understand how adipose tissue/fat plays a role in Lyme disease. We discovered that B. burgdorferi infection leads to an immune response in adipose tissue cells with specific downregulation of a gene called serum amyloid A (SAA). Our work shows that B. burgdorferi bacteria bind serum amyloid A (SAA), leading to decreased viability in vitro and enhanced uptake of B. burgdorferi by white blood cells. These findings highlight the dynamic role our fat can play during B. burgdorferi infection and can lead to the identification of new treatments for Lyme disease.

papers.title: Transcriptomic Characterization of a Monocyte Antigen-Presentation-Low Immunoparalysis State in Sepsis.
papers.authors: Wang Z, Tan Y, Ding J, Xie Y.
papers.abstract: Sepsis immunoparalysis is commonly monitored with monocyte HLA-DR, but whether a composite antigen-presentation-low transcriptomic state adds mechanistic information beyond existing endotypes remains uncertain. We integrated public bulk cohorts (GSE65682, GSE57065, and GSE54514) with single-cell datasets (GSE167363 and GSE279452) to define a directional immunoparalysis score combining low antigen-presentation/HLA-II and costimulatory response with high emergency-myeloid and inhibitory-tolerance programs. In GSE65682, the score was associated with 28-day mortality ( n = 479; adjusted OR = 1.32, 95% CI: 1.01-1.72; p = 0.0396), although discrimination was modest (AUC = 0.568, 95% CI: 0.506-0.628). The score overlapped with MARS endotypes, was highest in MARS2, and remained associated after age, sex, and MARS adjustment (OR = 1.39, 95% CI: 1.00-1.92; p = 0.048). GSE57065 supported disease-state elevation, whereas GSE54514 and APACHE II analyses defined negative predictive boundaries. Single-cell analyses localized the signal to antigen-presenting and pro-inflammatory monocytes, classical monocytes, and dendritic cells. The proposed transcript panel is hypothesis-generating for prospective immune-state monitoring, not a validated clinical decision tool.

papers.title: Macrophage Polarization in Sarcoidosis: Implications for Granuloma Formation, Fibrosis, and Therapeutic Strategies.
papers.authors: Shamaei M.
papers.abstract: Sarcoidosis is a multisystem granulomatous disease with a complex and incompletely understood immunopathogenesis. Macrophages and T lymphocytes play pivotal roles in granuloma formation and disease progression through dynamic interactions involving cytokine signaling and immune regulation. Recent evidence suggests that macrophage polarization, particularly the balance between classically activated M1 macrophages and alternatively activated M2 macrophages, plays a critical role in inflammatory granuloma formation and fibrotic progression in pulmonary sarcoidosis. TH1-related cytokines, including interferon-gamma (IFN-γ) and tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), promote proinflammatory M1 polarization, whereas TH2-related cytokines, such as interleukin (IL)-4 and IL-13, drive M2 polarization, tissue remodeling, and fibrosis. Emerging transcriptional, single-cell spatial transcriptomic, and 3D organoid studies further demonstrate the remarkable heterogeneity of macrophages in sarcoid granulomas. Current and emerging therapeutic approaches, including corticosteroids, methotrexate, anti-TNF agents, leflunomide, Janus kinase inhibitors, and novel macrophage-targeted strategies (such as efzofitimod), may exert their effects, in part, by modulating these distinct macrophage activation pathways. This review summarizes the available evidence on macrophage polarization in sarcoidosis and provides an immunology-informed clinical framework for disease endotyping, biomarker-guided monitoring, and targeted therapeutic strategies to prevent fibrotic progression.

papers.title: Pseudotime-Derived Seven-Gene Prognostic Signature and TYRP1 in Melanoma.
papers.authors: Li X, Deng Y, Song Y, Liu X, Li H.
papers.abstract: Background Melanoma is characterized by high malignancy and complex immune microenvironment heterogeneity. A robust prognostic framework that integrates tumor cell state diversity with clinical outcome remains lacking. Methods Integrative scRNA-seq analysis of public melanoma datasets was performed using Harmony batch correction, unsupervised clustering, and Monocle 3 pseudotime trajectory reconstruction to characterize tumor cell state transitions. Pseudotime-dynamic genes were subjected to univariate Cox screening across four independent cohorts (GSE19234, GSE22153, GSE65904, TCGA), followed by LASSO-Cox regression to construct a multigene prognostic model. Validation encompassed immune infiltration estimation, pathway activity scoring, tumor mutational burden (TMB) analysis, and protein-level expression assessment. Results scRNA-seq identified 14 major cell populations, within which tumor cell reclustering resolved seven functional states: melanocytic, neural crest-like, MHC-II high, stress/transitional, proliferating, IFN-stimulated, and invasive. Pseudotime analysis reconstructed a directional evolution trajectory originating from the melanocytic state, with the stress/transitional state acting as a central hub. Gene module enrichment further delineated the core transcriptional programs of each state. A seven-gene prognostic model (GBP4, ITGB4, GBP2, TNFSF13B, TSC22D3, CIITA, TYRP1) achieved consistent survival stratification across all four cohorts (all p p Conclusion This study presents an integrated single-cell and multicohort prognostic framework for melanoma, revealing the mechanistic link between tumor cell state evolution and immune microenvironment remodeling, and establishing TYRP1 as an independent prognostic biomarker to guide precision immunotherapy decision-making.

papers.title: Knockdown of a regulatory barcode shifts macrophage polarization destination from M1 to M2 and increases pathogen burden upon S. aureus infection.
papers.authors: Ravichandran S, Bhatt B, Shah A, Das D, Narayanaswamy Balaji K, Chandra N.
papers.abstract: Macrophages are driven to form distinct functional phenotypes in response to different immunological stimuli, in a process widely referred to as macrophage polarization. Transcriptional regulators that guide macrophage polarization in response to a given trigger remain largely unknown. In this study, we interrogate the programmable landscape in macrophages to find regulatory panels that determine the precise polarization state that a macrophage is driven to. Toward this, we configure an integrative network analysis pipeline that utilizes macrophage transcriptomes in response to 28 distinct stimuli, reconstructs contextualized human gene regulatory networks, and identifies epicenters of perturbations in each case. We find that these contextualized regulatory networks form a spectrum of 13 distinct clusters, with M1 and M2 at the two ends. Using our computational pipeline, we identify combinatorial panels of epicentric regulatory factors (RFs) for each polarization state. We demonstrate that a set of three RFs, that is, CEBPB , NFE2L2 , and BCL3 , is sufficient to change the polarization destination from M1 to M2. siRNA knockdown of the 3-RF-set in THP1-derived M0 cells, despite exposure to an M1 stimulant, significantly attenuated the shift to M1 phenotype and instead increased the expression of M2 markers. Single knockdown of each RF also showed a similar trend. The siRNA-mediated knockdown of the 3-RF-set rendered the macrophages hyper-susceptible to Staphylococcus aureus infection, demonstrating the importance of these factors in modulating immune responses. Overall, our results provide insights into the transcriptional mechanisms underlying macrophage polarization and identify key RFs that may be targeted to modulate immune responses.

papers.title: BATF-overexpressing Treg cell infusion attenuates experimental osteoarthritis by enhancing Treg immunoregulatory function.
papers.authors: Li H, Zhang R, Dong F, Gou X, Li F, Wang W.
papers.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a whole-joint degenerative disease characterized by progressive cartilage damage and persistent local immune dysregulation. Regulatory T cells (Tregs) contribute to immune homeostasis, but their functional heterogeneity and the molecular mechanisms governing their activity in OA remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to characterize Treg-cell heterogeneity in joint-associated tissues, investigate the role of basic leucine zipper ATF-like transcription factor (BATF) in regulating Treg function, and evaluate whether BATF overexpression enhances the therapeutic activity of adoptively transferred Treg cells in experimental OA. Public bulk transcriptomic and single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets were analyzed to characterize disease-associated immune alterations, chondrocyte states, and synovial Treg-cell heterogeneity. BATF was overexpressed or knocked out in mouse Treg cells, followed by analyses of proliferation, IL-10 and TGF-β1 secretion, and suppression of Th17-cell proliferation. ChIP-qPCR, dual-luciferase reporter assays, qRT-PCR, and Western blotting were used to examine the potential BATF-IL-2RB-JAK1/STAT5 regulatory relationship. FOXP3/BATF double immunofluorescence was performed to assess BATF-positive Treg cells in control and OA joint tissues. The therapeutic effects of BATF-overexpressing Treg cells were evaluated in papain- and DMM-induced OA models. An empty-vector-transfected Treg-cell group was included in the papain-induced model to distinguish the effects of BATF overexpression from those of Treg-cell transfer itself. Transcriptomic analyses identified disease-associated inflammatory alterations and impaired Treg-related immune features, while single-cell analysis revealed functionally heterogeneous synovial Treg populations. BATF-high Treg cells displayed stronger immunosuppressive transcriptional characteristics. FOXP3/BATF double immunofluorescence showed a reduced abundance of FOXP3⁺BATF⁺ Treg cells in OA joint tissues compared with controls. In vitro, BATF overexpression enhanced Treg-cell proliferation, increased IL-10 and TGF-β1 secretion, and strengthened suppression of Th17-cell proliferation, whereas BATF knockout produced opposite effects. ChIP-qPCR, promoter-reporter assays, and signaling analyses supported an association between BATF-mediated IL-2RB transcription and JAK1-STAT5 activation. In vivo, BATF-overexpressing Treg-cell transfer attenuated cartilage degeneration, preserved Collagen II and Aggrecan expression, and improved the local inflammatory cytokine profile. In the papain-induced OA model, these effects were greater than those observed following NC-Treg transfer. BATF is associated with an enhanced immunosuppressive phenotype of Treg cells and may contribute to their functional regulation partly through the IL-2RB/JAK1-STAT5 signaling axis. BATF overexpression enhanced the therapeutic activity of adoptively transferred Treg cells in experimental OA, supporting further investigation of functionally engineered Treg cells as a potential immune-modulatory strategy for OA. Further studies are required to validate the underlying mechanism in vivo and thoroughly evaluate potential side effects, off-target tissue distribution, long-term phenotypic stability, and the translational safety of this engineered cell therapy.

papers.title: Neoadjuvant botensilimab with or without balstilimab in pMMR and dMMR colon cancer: the phase 2 UNICORN trial.
papers.authors: Ghelardi F, Ambrosini M, Raimondi A, Tyshevich A, Palermo F, Bergamo F, Nasca V, Manca P, Mulas I, Derosa L, Brown G, Chiodoni C, Di Maio M, Di Donato S, Chiaramonte A, Castagnoli L, Ni S, Nousome D, Spickard E, Tin A, Lentz R, Jurdi A, Sabella G, Spada D, Tamberi S, Passardi A, Morano F, Tamburini E, Rossi C, Azzolin L, Cambuli F, Martinetti A, Sottotetti E, Almonte AA, Iebba V, Ratti C, Cerantola R, Kutlu Ö, Cristarella E, Pupa SM, Villa C, Perissinotto E, Galassi M, Barina A, Vittadello F, Guaglio M, Baiocchi G, Sartore-Bianchi A, Rosati R, Cremolini C, Montroni I, Lonardi S, Sottoriva A, Pietrantonio F.
papers.abstract: Preoperative immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) are active in patients with deficient mismatch repair (dMMR) colon cancer (CC), whereas proficient mismatch repair (pMMR) CC has been consistently considered resistant to first-generation ICIs. In the phase 2 UNICORN trial, we evaluated short-course preoperative botensilimab (BOT; multifunctional Fc-enhanced anti-CTLA-4 monoclonal antibody) alone or in combination with the anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody balstilimab (BOT + BAL) in 56 patients with resectable, locally advanced CC. Twenty-eight patients with pMMR CC were sequentially enrolled in BOT (n = 14) and BOT + BAL (n = 14) cohorts. Twenty-eight patients with dMMR CC followed the same sequential allocation strategy. The primary endpoint of centrally assessed pathological major response (pMR) rate (≤10% of residual viable tumor) was met in all cohorts, except pMMR BOT. Specifically, the pMR rate was 0% (95% confidence interval (CI): 0-23.2%) in pMMR BOT, 36% (95% CI: 12.8-64.9%) in pMMR BOT + BAL, 36% (95% CI: 12.8-64.9%) in dMMR BOT and 100% (95% CI: 76.8-100%) in dMMR BOT + BAL. Secondary endpoints included safety, quality of life, describing treatment-induced transcriptional dynamics, peripheral blood mononuclear cell dynamics, radiomics and radiogenomics features, fecal microbiota composition and circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) dynamics. Eight (29%) and 15 (54%) patients treated with BOT and BOT + BAL, respectively, experienced immune-related adverse events, most commonly flu-like syndrome and diarrhea. Single-cell spatial transcriptomic analysis of matched baseline and post-treatment samples highlighted high baseline PD-L1 stromal expression and low post-treatment regulatory T cell signatures in pMMR responders, whereas dMMR responders displayed high baseline FCGR2A and FCGR3A expression on intratumoral macrophages. Clearance of ctDNA before surgery correlated with pathological response and lack of recurrence at data cutoff. Preoperative BOT + BAL elicits pathological responses in patients with pMMR or dMMR CC, supporting the combination as a promising strategy to expand ICI benefits to the early-stage setting. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05845450 .

papers.title: Research progress of biomarkers in Sjögren disease.
papers.authors: Dang M, Yang M, Li J.
papers.abstract: Sjögren disease is a chronic autoimmune disorder characterized by immune-mediated dysregulation that leads to exocrine gland destruction, impaired tissue repair, and frequent co-occurrence with other connective tissue diseases. Current internationally accepted diagnostic criteria rely predominantly on a combination of characteristic clinical manifestations, autoantibody profiles, and histopathological findings from minor salivary gland biopsy. In early-stage disease, when immune-driven glandular injury has not yet caused evident structural damage, or when histopathological alterations are delayed compared to clinical symptoms, the conventional "gold standard" method may produce false-negative outcomes, leading to diagnostic delays or overlooked diagnoses. In recent years, advances in multi-omics platforms, single-cell technologies, and artificial intelligence-driven data analysis have enabled the discovery of a growing number of promising biomarkers, including proteases, metabolites, microRNAs, and novel autoantibody epitopes detectable in serum, saliva, and tears. Several of these candidates have already undergone translational validation and are beginning to impact clinical decision-making. This review highlights recent advancements in biomarker research for Sjögren disease, evaluating their diagnostic utility, prognostic relevance, and therapeutic implications.

papers.title: Hepatic Stellate Cells: Fibrogenic Effectors to Central Regulators of Metabolism, Liver Disease Signaling, and Systemic Crosstalk.
papers.authors: Li X, Chen H, Fu W.
papers.abstract: Hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) have long been regarded as the core effector cells in liver fibrosis. The advent of single-cell omics and metabolomics has led to a paradigm shift in our understanding of these cells. Notably, they are not only implicated in local fibrosis but are being increasingly recognized as a hub integrating metabolic and immune signaling. Located at the interface between hepatic vasculature and parenchyma, HSCs have the capacity to modulate intestinal barrier function, neurotransmitter circulation, myocardial energy metabolism, and bone remodeling through metabolic reprogramming (enhanced glycolysis, vitamin A consumption, glutamine metabolism remodeling) and receptor signaling (TLR4, TGF-β, CXCR4, etc.), as well as by secreting metabolites, exosomal miRNAs, and cytokines. Concurrently, HSCs perceive feedback signals from these organs, forming a dynamic cross-organ feedback network. This review systematically integrates the metabolic characteristics of HSCs in diseases such as metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, alcohol-related liver disease, chronic viral hepatitis, and hepatocellular carcinoma, along with their cross-organ interactive effects. We further discuss intervention strategies targeting metabolic pathways, exosomal cargo, and the microbiota-metabolism axis, and propose a three-tier translational framework stratifying HSC-targeted therapeutic approaches by developmental stage, offering novel insights for shifting liver disease treatment from single antifibrotic approaches toward systemic, multi-organ precision interventions.

papers.title: TIM3 Blockade with Hypomethylating Therapy Restores NK Cell and Cytotoxic CD4+ T-cell Activity in Patients with AML or MDS.
papers.authors: Huuhtanen J, Forstén S, Ford B, Smolander J, Brück O, Lundgren S, Kreutzman A, Dufva O, Kankainen M, Ilander M, Lähteenmäki H, Kasanen T, Klievink J, Leitner J, Steinberger P, Kontro M, Pelletier MR, Lähdesmäki H, Sabatos-Peyton C, Rinne ML, Porkka K, Peltonen K, Mustjoki S.
papers.abstract: Occasional complete responses (CR) to immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy demonstrate that acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) can be immunosensitive when appropriately targeted. In this study, we analyzed patients with AML/MDS (n = 14) who were treated with the anti-TIM3 sabatolimab and the hypomethylating agent decitabine in a phase Ib clinical trial (NCT03066648) using single-cell RNA and T-cell receptor (TCR) sequencing (n = 6) and functional coculture assays. Unlike T cell-restricted CTLA4 and PD1, TIM3 was broadly expressed across natural killer (NK) cell, myeloid cell, and T-cell populations. Therapy induced the expansion of cytotoxic NK cell subsets and enhanced type I IFN signaling. Fewer than 1% of bone marrow CD8+ T cells displayed a canonical exhaustion phenotype, and treatment preferably expanded small CD8+ T-cell clones in responders. Responders exhibited greater expansion of cytotoxic CD4+ T cells and B cells, as exemplified by a patient with preexisting CD4+ T-cell large granular lymphocyte leukemia (T-LGLL) achieving an outstanding CR lasting 23 months. More than 20% of this patient's lymphocytes were T-LGLL cells expressing a TCR capable of recognizing autologous blasts. Overall, our results suggest that anti-TIM3 combined with decitabine engages a distinct mechanism of immune activation compared with anti-PD-1 and anti-CTLA4, preferentially expanding NK cell and CD4+ T-cell populations.

papers.title: Multiomics Dissection of Early-Onset Colorectal Cancer (EOCRC) Reveals an Immunosuppressive Microenvironment and Identifies FAT3 Mutation as a Biomarker of Hot-Like Immune Features.
papers.authors: Wang L, Lu Y, Ma W, Guo J, Zhang W, Shi Y.
papers.abstract: Early-onset colorectal cancer (EOCRC) exhibits distinct clinical and biological features compared with late-onset CRC (LOCRC), yet its genomic architecture and immune microenvironmental determinants remain incompletely characterized. Here, we integrated multiomics discovery analyses of 69 EOCRC and 461 LOCRC patients from the TCGA cohort, complemented by independent validation, single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and systems-level network analysis. We identified 10 genes significantly enriched for mutations in EOCRC, including ANXA7, ZNF267, and POLQ, which displayed distinct domain-specific clustering and were validated in an external cohort. Mutational signature decomposition showed that EOCRC was associated with an SBS87-like signature, whereas LOCRC was dominated by SBS1; because TCGA lacks detailed treatment history, this SBS87-like inference should not be interpreted as direct evidence of prior thiopurine exposure. Immunologically, EOCRC displayed an immunosuppressive microenvironment characterized by elevated regulatory T cells, resting NK cells, and tighter immune-stromal coupling, as further supported by spatial transcriptomic analysis. Single-cell atlas analysis identified M2-polarized, SPP1-expressing macrophage subsets in EOCRC. Weighted gene coexpression network analysis identified a mitochondrial-ribosomal biogenesis module as the transcriptional hallmark of EOCRC. Finally, random forest analysis identified FAT3 mutations as a genomic correlate of a hot-like, immune-activated phenotype in EOCRC. Integrative single-cell analysis localized FAT3 predominantly to cancer-associated fibroblasts, especially myofibroblasts, and an in silico FAT3 perturbation analysis suggested potential downstream programs involving extracellular matrix remodeling, inflammatory signaling, chemokine response, and mitotic spindle regulation. These findings delineate age-stratified genomic and microenvironmental features of EOCRC and generate testable hypotheses for future functional and clinical validation.
