papers.title: An Immune-Metabolic Signature Reveals Prognostic Stratification and Tumor Microenvironment Features in Breast Cancer.
papers.authors: Dong S, Xu W, Liu S, Zhang K, Deng K, Li Z, Ren H.
papers.abstract: Breast cancer progression reflects coupled immune and metabolic reprogramming, but biomarkers that capture this interplay and provide additional prognostic information beyond routine clinicopathological assessment remain limited. We developed an 11-gene immune-metabolic risk Score in TCGA-BRCA (n = 1099) by integrating C7 immune signatures and KEGG metabolic pathways through Cox and LASSO-Cox modeling. The fixed model was applied without retraining to three public cohorts and an independent institutional cohort of 146 patients from Harbin Medical University Cancer Hospital. The score consistently stratified overall survival across independent cohorts and provided additional prognostic information beyond conventional clinicopathological variables. Integrative analyses showed that high-risk tumors were characterized by enhanced cell-cycle and metabolic activation, reduced lymphocyte-associated immune features, and monocytic-lineage enrichment. At single-cell resolution, high-score cancer-associated fibroblasts exhibited enhanced extracellular-matrix remodeling, inflammatory iCAF activity, and TGF-β-associated immunosuppressive programs. In an exploratory pembrolizumab-containing cohort, lower pretreatment scores were associated with pathological complete response and immune-active transcriptional programs; however, these findings do not establish the score as a predictive biomarker for immunotherapy benefit. The 11-gene immune-metabolic risk Score provides complementary prognostic stratification beyond conventional clinical variables and characterizes a stromal-remodeled immune-metabolic state associated with adverse breast cancer outcomes.

papers.title: 6PPD-Quinone Promotes Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease through Immune-Inflammatory Disruption.
papers.authors: Zuo X, Ma L, Hou X, Zhang C, Tan S, Zhang Y, Pu Y, Zhang J.
papers.abstract: 6PPD-quinone (6PPDQ), a transformation product of the tire antioxidant 6PPD, is widely detected in environmental and human matrices, yet its relevance to metabolic liver disease remains unclear. We examined its potential contribution to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) by integrating disease-burden analysis, computational toxicology, human transcriptomics, and cross-model validation. The intersection of predicted 6PPDQ targets with MASLD transcriptomic signatures identified 103 candidate genes enriched predominantly in immune and inflammatory pathways. Three machine-learning algorithms prioritized six hub genes, ASPM, ERN1, GADD45B, GINS2, LDLR, and MYPOP, which discriminated MASLD from controls with a combined AUC of 0.997. Immune deconvolution and single-cell analyses were associated with this signature with hepatic immune remodeling and intercellular communication. Molecular docking and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations predicted stable interactions between 6PPDQ and several targets, particularly ERN1. Environmentally informed low-dose oral exposure produced hepatic steatosis, inflammation, and injury in mice, while LC-MS/MS confirmed internal exposure. Concordant transcriptional responses were reproduced in the hiPSC-derived liver organoids. Integration of these findings supported a provisional adverse outcome pathway linking 6PPDQ exposure to MASLD-related liver injuries. Collectively, these results implicate 6PPDQ as a plausible environmental hazard for metabolic liver injury and support expanding the risk assessment of tire-derived contaminants beyond that of aquatic ecotoxicity.

papers.title: Macrophage-directed immunotherapy in Inflammatory bowel disease: advances in reprogramming intestinal phagocytes.
papers.authors: Shao Y, Yu S.
papers.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic, relapsing inflammatory disorder characterized by dysregulation of the intestinal immune system, in which functional abnormalities of phagocytes such as macrophages play a critical role in pathogenesis. Although conventional therapies such as anti-tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) antibodies are widely used in clinical practice, they have limitations including low response rates and significant side effects, creating an urgent need for novel therapeutic strategies. In recent years, macrophage-directed immunotherapy has emerged as a cutting-edge approach for IBD treatment by reprogramming intestinal phagocytes to restore immune homeostasis. Unlike previous reviews that primarily focus on the M1/M2 polarization framework, this review integrates recent single-cell discoveries of novel macrophage subsets (e.g. SPP1 + and TREM2 + macrophages), systematically examines the crosstalk among signaling, epigenetic, and metabolic regulatory layers, and critically evaluates translational barriers from preclinical models to clinical application. By evaluating preclinical and clinical studies, we assess the potential and challenges of these strategies. Through in-depth analysis, this review aims to provide a theoretical basis for the development of more precise and effective immunotherapies for IBD and to point out future research directions. (Literature search: PubMed, Web of Science, and Embase; January 2000-December 2025.).

papers.title: Fasting-Mimicking Diets Reprogram Cancer-Associated Fibroblasts to Reverse the Immunosuppressive Tumor Microenvironment in Breast Cancer.
papers.authors: Zhang J, Li N, Li R, Chen Y, Ashby CR, Tang Y, Sun Y, Xie X, Chen ZS, Yang L.
papers.abstract: Fasting-mimicking diets (FMD) have been reported to increase the antitumor efficacy in preclinical studies in various cancers. FMD can affect the tumor microenvironment (TME), and elucidating the mechanisms and cells mediating the effects of FMD may uncover combination treatment strategies. Here, we performed single-cell transcriptomic sequencing to characterize the TME changes induced by FMD intervention in a mouse model of spontaneous breast cancer. The sequencing data indicated that FMD suppressed tumor cell stemness, promoted apoptosis, and increased the infiltration of innate and adaptive immune cells, especially natural killer (NK) cells and effector CD8+ T cells. Importantly, FMD induced phenotypic reprogramming of cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAF), leading to a decrease in the immunosuppressive inflammatory CAF (iCAF) subset. Mechanistically, FMD decreased platelet-derived growth factor C (PDGFC) secretion in tumor cells by reducing glucose levels and inhibiting glycolysis to reprogram CAFs. PDGFC increased the activation of the JAK-STAT3 pathway, which induced iCAF differentiation. Combining FMD with PDGF receptor (PDGFR) inhibitors increased the efficacy of anti-PD-L1 immunotherapy in vivo. Overall, this study reveals a mechanism of metabolic-immune rewiring through which FMD suppresses tumor progression, providing preliminary evidence for the potential of combination FMD-based strategies in breast cancer treatment. Significance Fasting-mimicking diet blocks breast cancer cell-induced generation of immunosuppressive fibroblasts, thereby facilitating tumor infiltration of immune cells and stimulating antitumor immunity to sensitize breast cancer to immunotherapy.

papers.title: Spatial Profiling Reveals Immune Escape Pathways and Therapeutic Vulnerabilities in Prostate Cancer Bone Metastases.
papers.authors: Owen KL, Gearing LJ, Niranjan B, Jayawardana M, Chadwick TB, Newman HI, Weng S, Trigos AS, Devereux LM, Campbell BK, Pasam A, Corcoran NM, Taylor RA, Hovens CM, Hertzog PJ, Sandhu S, Haynes NM, Parker BS.
papers.abstract: Prostate cancer frequently metastasizes to bone, marking incurable disease. This progression is driven by an immunologically cold bone tumor microenvironment that fosters resistance to therapy. To define the mechanisms underlying this uniquely immunosuppressive niche, we applied spatial single-cell analyses across primary tumors and metastatic sites. Bone metastases showed marked suppression of tumor-intrinsic type I interferon (IFN-I) signaling and loss of antigen presentation, features that were strongly associated with reduced bone metastasis-free survival. Tumor-intrinsic IFN-I expression correlated with memory T-cell infiltration, whereas the bone myeloid compartment was enriched for protumor macrophages and showed reduced dendritic cell activation and antigen presentation. Digital spatial profiling of matched tumors revealed a broad loss of IFN-I-regulated immunostimulatory and checkpoint molecules. Notably, B7-H3, a putative negative regulator of IFN-I, was highly expressed in bone metastases and inversely associated with antigen presentation. These findings define bone-specific mechanisms of immune resistance and highlight therapeutic vulnerabilities that could inform precision therapeutic strategies for prostate cancer. Significance Prostate cancer bone metastases establish a tumor-driven, immunosuppressive niche featuring global impairment of IFN-I signaling and antigen presentation coupled to elevated B7-H3, highlighting clinically actionable vulnerabilities in advanced prostate cancer.

papers.title: COL1A1-Mediated BMP1-TGF-β Signaling Augments EMT and M2 Macrophage Polarization in Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
papers.authors: Liu X, Li Y, Gao L, Lu R, Fang Y, Yang X.
papers.abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is a lethal malignancy characterized by frequent metastasis. Utilizing a 4-nitroquinoline 1-oxide-induced murine model and single-cell RNA sequencing, we identified a distinct collagen type I alpha 1 chain (Col1a1+) epithelial subpopulation that is significantly expanded in OSCC, exhibits the highest epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) signature, and correlates with poor patient survival. Functional studies demonstrated that Col1a1 knockdown (KD) in OSCC cell lines (HSC3, SCC25) attenuated transforming growth factor β (TGF-β)-induced EMT, impaired migration and invasion in vitro, and reduced tumor burden in a conditional knockout mouse model. Transcriptomic profiling following Col1a1 silencing revealed the suppression of TGF-β signaling and extracellular matrix (ECM)-receptor interaction pathways. We further identified BMP1 as a key downstream effector, demonstrating a direct physical interaction between COL1A1 and BMP1, and showed that COL1A1 potentiates BMP1's proteolytic activity. Rescue experiments confirmed that BMP1 is essential for COL1A1-driven tumor growth, metastasis, and TGF-β pathway activation in vivo. Furthermore, we uncovered an immunomodulatory role for the COL1A1-BMP1 axis, whereby it promotes M2 macrophage polarization via TGF-β secretion to foster an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. This effect was reversible using either BMP1-KD or TGF-β neutralization. In conclusion, our study establishes a novel COL1A1-BMP1-TGF-β signaling cascade that drives OSCC progression by autonomously enhancing tumor cell malignancy and nonautonomously reprogramming the immune landscape, nominating this axis as a promising therapeutic target. Implications These findings identify a novel COL1A1-BMP1 axis driving both OSCC malignancy and immunosuppression, offering potential diagnostic markers and therapeutic targets for the clinic.

papers.title: Tumor Microbial Burden Drives Immune Responses through Regulation of Interferon Signaling.
papers.authors: Liu H, Jang JH, Peng F, Rajaei H, Chandra V, Li L, Rupani DN, Taghinezhadsaroukalaei S, Zhao Y, Faraoni EY, Bartelli TF, Le Roux O, Tahan V, Jimenez-Arancon F, Baydogan S, Mohseni AH, Gomez JA, Patel M, Burks JK, Miño Galvez B, Carvajal-Hausdorf DE, Ruiz-García E, Fernandez-Figueroa EA, Kopetz S, Maron SB, Cercek A, Riquelme EM, Navin NE, White JR, Wang L, Diaz LA, McAllister F.
papers.abstract: Tumor microbes are increasingly recognized for modulating tumor behavior and therapy responses. Intratumoral microbial burden (ITMB) analysis across cancers revealed regulation of immune pathways and activated mast cells, mostly in colorectal and gastric cancers. High-ITMB colorectal cancer leads to interferon (IFN) regulation and is associated with improved outcomes in advanced disease. Single-cell sequencing revealed induction of IFN-related genes (IRG) within microbe-containing human colorectal cancer. Gastrointestinal-luminal mismatch repair-deficient (MMRd) tumors had higher ITMB than proficient tumors. In a rectal MMRd cohort with 100% remission after immune checkpoint blockade (ICB), tumor microbes and microbe-containing mast cells increased. In ICB-sensitive syngeneic murine MMRd tumor models, local tumor microbial depletion impaired ICB efficacy while downregulating IFN signaling. Forced upregulation of IRGs in ADAR1-deficient cancer cells restored immunotherapy responses during microbial ablation. These data highlight dynamic interplay among ITMB, host defense, and immunogenicity, which seems key to determine therapy responses. Significance The ITMB is linked to transcriptional and immune functional changes that seem to determine tumor sensitivity to immunotherapy. These findings highlight the key role of tumor-resident microbes in shaping the tumor ecosystem, which could be targeted to modulate therapy responses.

papers.title: H2AFY2 Suppresses Exhaustion and Enhances Antitumor Activity of CAR T Cells through Transcriptional and Epigenetic Modifications.
papers.authors: Li C, Wang Q, Zhao Q, Cai Q, Wang S, Ping Y, Zhao X, Chen X, Shen C, Qin H, Qin G, Shan J, Zhang Z, Zhang Y.
papers.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell exhaustion constitutes a critical barrier to sustained antitumor efficacy. Through transcriptomic analysis of CAR T cells from patients with lymphoma, we identified the histone variant macroH2A2 (H2AFY2) as a critical regulator of T-cell exhaustion-a finding consistently observed across multiple tumor models. In mice, T cell-specific knockout of H2afy2 promotes the expression of inhibitory receptors by activating the NF-κB pathway and increasing chromatin accessibility at the Rela locus, as demonstrated by single-cell RNA sequencing and Assay for Transposase-Accessible Chromatin using sequencing. H2AFY2 overexpression in CD8+ T cells induces prominent epigenetic remodeling, characterized by increased H3K27me3 enrichment. Mechanistically, H3K27me3 enrichment at the Rela locus suppresses p65-mediated transcriptional activation, leading to downregulation of the exhaustion-associated transcription factor TOX and consequent amelioration of T-cell exhaustion. Furthermore, H2AFY2-overexpressing CAR T cells sustain lower levels of inhibitory receptors and suppress tumor recurrence. Collectively, these results define an epigenetic pathway through which H2AFY2 counteracts T-cell exhaustion and supports the therapeutic potential of H2AFY2-engineered CAR T cells across tumor types.

papers.title: The Posttranscriptional Regulator HuR Promotes Immune Evasion in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma.
papers.authors: Guo Y, Finan JM, Bartlett AQ, Pelz KR, Sivagnanam S, Blise KE, Kirchberger N, Betre K, Wei Y, Eng JR, Shah VM, Chin K, McCarthy GA, Halamish H, MacPherson-Hawthorne K, Daniel CJ, Chen C, Grossberg AJ, Xia Z, Cao S, Coussens LM, Sears RC, Brody JR, Eil R.
papers.abstract: The tumor microenvironment (TME) of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is characterized by the restrained function of effector T cells that drive resistance to immunotherapy. Although tumor-extrinsic stroma and myeloid cells have been shown to mediate PDAC immune evasion, the role of tumor-intrinsic posttranscriptional gene regulation in driving tumor-immune cross-talk has been relatively unexplored. In this study, we report that the RNA-binding protein human antigen R (HuR; ELAVL1) is enriched in human PDAC and negatively correlates with T-cell infiltration. In two immunocompetent murine models of PDAC, we found that genetic disruption of HuR impaired tumor growth without significantly affecting in vivo proliferation. Comprehensive spatial and flow cytometry profiling of the PDAC TME revealed that genetic disruption of HuR in PDAC enhanced both T-cell number and functional state. Moreover, T-cell depletion abrogated the growth difference caused by HuR loss. Mechanistically, RNA immunoprecipitation sequencing, single-cell RNA sequencing, and orthogonal functional assays in vitro and in vivo showed that HuR stabilized mTOR pathway transcripts critical for metabolic adaptation in PDAC. HuR-driven metabolic reprogramming promoted tumor nutrient dominance and limited nutrient consumption by neighboring tumor-reactive T cells. Accordingly, HuR depletion sensitized PDAC tumors to immune checkpoint blockade and allowed for the expansion of tumor-specific T-cell populations, suggesting that HuR-mediated nutrient dominance and immune evasion have translational relevance. Overall, we found that the posttranscriptional regulator HuR facilitates immune evasion in PDAC by constraining T-cell function, identifying HuR blockade as a promising therapeutic strategy in combination with immunotherapies.

papers.title: RHOA Deletion Downregulates CD19 and Promotes Dysfunctional Immune Microenvironments in CAR T-Resistant Large B-cell Lymphomas.
papers.authors: Newsam AD, Ziccheddu B, Youssfi AA, Venkatarame Gowda Saralamma V, Foos-Russ S, Tsai DE, Sheffield-Veney I, Jeevan A, Manara P, Goretsky YE, Suissa DM, Russo MV, Fattakhov N, Carmona-Berrio D, Campos Gallego N, Coughlin CA, Sondhi AK, Roberts ER, Spiegel JY, Alderuccio JP, Amador C, Bilbao D, Coffey DG, Jain MD, Maura F, Locke FL, Schatz JH.
papers.abstract: CD19-directed chimeric antigen receptor (CAR-19) T cells are breakthrough therapies for large B-cell lymphomas (LBCL), but fewer than half of patients achieve durable responses. We previously showed that RHOA deletions are enriched in progressing cases, but the role of RHOA deficiency is poorly defined despite its frequent occurrence in newly diagnosed disease. In this study, we show that RHOA loss downregulates CD19, promoting cell-intrinsic resistance to CAR-19 in vitro and in vivo. CD19 decline, however, provides an incomplete explanation of resistance and does not explain high frequency of the deletion in newly diagnosed cases. We therefore performed single-cell assessments of immunocompetent RHOA-deficient lymphoma microenvironments (LME), revealing remarkable concordance with features in CAR-19-resistant patients. Despite increased microenvironmental production of interferon gamma, RHOA-deficient tumor cells themselves show an impaired response to the cytokine, including failed induction of class I MHC molecules. Overall, we describe for the first time how a single-gene alteration recurrent in CAR-19-resistant lymphoma contributes to treatment failures. Significance RHOA loss of function, which predicts CAR T-cell treatment failure and is present in one in six newly diagnosed LBCL cases, impairs MHC class I display, reprograms LMEs, and downregulates CD19 to promote antigen escape. Del 3p21.31 is therefore a single-gene alteration in LBCL selected for immunotherapy resistance. See related commentary by Perkey and Kline, p. 852.

papers.title: Stromal CD163-positive Macrophage Enrichment Is Associated With a FOXP3-skewed Immune Profile and Poor Prognosis in Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
papers.authors: Jiao W, Lv F, Liu X, Wang D, Han J, Yamada S, Liu Y.
papers.abstract: Background/aim The prognostic significance of macrophage-centered spatial immune architecture in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) remains incompletely understood. We investigated the spatial distribution and prognostic relevance of CD163-positive macrophages and their association with T-cell subsets in ESCC. Materials and methods A total of 139 patients with surgically resected ESCC, including a primary cohort (n=89) and an independent validation cohort (n=50), were analyzed. Double immunofluorescence staining was performed to evaluate CD163-positive macrophages, CD8-positive T cells, and FOXP3-positive T cells in intratumoral and stromal compartments. Associations with clinicopathological features and overall survival were assessed. Public transcriptomic and single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets were analyzed for external biological validation. Results CD163-positive macrophages, CD8-positive T cells, and FOXP3-positive T cells were predominantly enriched in the stromal compartment. Stromal CD163-positive macrophage infiltration was positively associated with both CD8-positive and FOXP3-positive T-cell infiltration and with an increased stromal FOXP3/CD8 ratio, indicating an inflamed but FOXP3-skewed immune phenotype. Compared to conventional T-cell-based indicators, stromal CD163-related immune features showed stronger and more consistent associations with poor overall survival and remained significantly associated with overall survival after adjustment for age and pathological TNM stage in separate multivariable models. These findings were reproduced in the validation cohort and supported by transcriptomic and single-cell analyses. Conclusion Stromal CD163-positive macrophage enrichment is associated with a FOXP3-skewed immune architecture and unfavorable prognosis in ESCC. Macrophage-centered spatial immune features may provide complementary prognostic information beyond conventional T-cell-based indicators and warrant further investigation.

figure.caption: Representative double immunofluorescence images showing the spatial distribution of immune-cell subsets in ESCC. Images were obtained from the invasive tumor front and adjacent tumor-associated stroma. (A) CD3-positive T cells (green) and FOXP3-positive T cells (red). (B) CD3-positive T cells (green) and CD8-positive T cells (red). (C) CD68-positive macrophages (green) and CD163-positive macrophages (red). Cell nuclei were counterstained with DAPI (blue). Merged images demonstrate marker co-localization and were used to facilitate identification of the corresponding immune-cell subsets. Images were acquired at ×200 magnification. Scale bar = 200 μm.
