papers.title: Identification of Potential Biomarkers for Ulcerative Colitis and Analysis of Immune Cell Infiltration: A Study Based on Data-Independent Acquisition Proteomics and the GEO Public Database.
papers.authors: Wang S, Deng H, Sun D.
papers.abstract: Background Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a challenging inflammatory bowel disease characterized by chronic inflammation of the colon's mucosal layer. Despite advances in medical research, UC lacks definitive diagnostic tests and targeted treatments. Aims This study aimed to preliminarily explore non-invasive potential biomarkers for UC based on proteomic analysis and publicly available GEO datasets. Materials & methods Bioinformatics analyses including ssGSEA for immune infiltration assessment, Spearman correlation analysis, ROC analysis, GSEA, and in silico drug prediction were performed. Results Four candidate hub genes (KRT17, TCEA3, ACP5, and ACOT13) were identified. ROC analysis demonstrated their potential clinical diagnostic value, and GSEA revealed their association with inflammatory pathways. A total of 28 potential compounds targeting these biomarkers were predicted, among which cinacalcet was selected as a priority candidate drug for further research. Conclusion The identified hub genes have the potential to act as non-invasive candidate biomarkers for the early diagnosis of UC.

papers.title: Monoclonal Antibody Coformulations Reveal Three Interaction Patterns Governing Stability.
papers.authors: Kalejaye LA, Shah M, Gallegos A, Mody N, Lai PK.
papers.abstract: Coformulated monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) offer a promising next-generation therapeutic strategy by combining multiple antibodies in a single drug product to enhance efficacy and improve patient compliance. However, ensuring the quality and stability of individual components in combination remains a key challenge. Here, we systematically characterized ten IgG1 mAbs (eight low-viscosity and two high-viscosity mAbs at 150 mg/mL) and all 45 possible 1:1 binary coformulations. Viscosity measurements revealed three distinct cross-interaction patterns: (1) minimal cross-interaction, where coformulation viscosity fell between those of the parental mAbs; (2) attractive cross-interaction, characterized by viscosity above both parental mAbs; and (3) repulsive cross-interaction, characterized by viscosity below both parental mAbs. Among the two high-viscosity mAbs, one exhibited reduced viscosity when coformulated with low-viscosity mAbs, whereas the other exhibited increased viscosity. Diffusion interaction parameter (kD) measurements showed partial correspondence with the observed interaction patterns, although kD did not consistently align with the viscosity trends across all coformulation pairs. In parallel, conformational stability was assessed using thermal unfolding parameters, including onset temperature (Tonset) and the first unfolding transition temperature (Tm1). Most coformulations exhibited thermal unfolding parameters intermediate between those of their parental mAbs, often shifting toward the less conformationally stable parent, indicating that conformational stability was generally retained following coformulation. This study represents one of the most comprehensive investigations of antibody coformulations to date and, to our knowledge, is the first to report repulsive interactions, particularly in the context of high-concentration viscosity. These findings highlight fundamental protein-protein interaction patterns that govern antibody coformulations, expand the knowledge base for the development of stable next-generation antibody combination therapies, and provide a rich experimental dataset to guide future computational modeling of mAb-mAb coformulation behavior.

papers.title: SLC9A3R1 Promotes Bladder Cancer Progression Through Regulation of Malignant Phenotypes: Integrated Bioinformatics Analysis and Experimental Validation.
papers.authors: Wang Y, Wu X, Shu C, Bao T.
papers.abstract: Background SLC9A3R1 is a PDZ domain-containing scaffolding protein, but its role in bladder cancer remains unclear. Methods This study analyzed publicly available pan-cancer datasets to characterize the expression patterns and prognostic significance of SLC9A3R1, and further explored its associated biological processes, pathways, and immune cell infiltration via differential expression, enrichment, and CIBERSORT analyses. Functional knockdown experiments in bladder cancer cell lines were also performed to assess the impact of SLC9A3R1 silencing on mTOR signaling and cellular activities. Results SLC9A3R1 was abnormally expressed across multiple tumor types, and its prognostic value differed among tumors. High SLC9A3R1 expression was linked to worse clinical outcomes in several distinct bladder cancer cohorts. SLC9A3R1-associated gene profiles were linked to immunological control, metabolic activities, cell cycle regulation, DNA replication and repair, and epithelial differentiation, according to functional enrichment analysis. CIBERSORT analysis further revealed associations between SLC9A3R1 expression and the infiltration levels of multiple immune cell populations in bladder cancer. SLC9A3R1 knockdown was shown to inhibit bladder cancer cell migration and proliferation in vitro, along with decreased levels of p-mTOR and p-S6. Conclusions SLC9A3R1 may promote bladder cancer progression through mTOR signaling and represents a potential prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target.

papers.title: H3K9me3 Regulates IFNγlow Tex Cell Differentiation to Promote Colon Tumor Liver Metastasis.
papers.authors: Fick K, Zhao Y, Tiamiyu Z, Czabala P, Poschel DB, Yang D, Yu M, Zoccheddu M, Bombin S, Liu K.
papers.abstract: Despite the breakthrough in immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) immunotherapy in human cancer, colon cancer, except for the small subset of microsatellite instable human colon cancer, does not respond to ICI immunotherapy. As liver metastasis accounts for more than 90% of human colon cancer cases and mortality, ICI efficacy is primarily a measurement of liver metastasis suppression. Using a colon tumor liver metastasis syngeneic mouse model, we determined that mouse colon tumor liver metastases not only do not respond to anti-PD-1 immunotherapy but also exhibit no susceptibility to tumor-specific cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL) adoptive transfer immunotherapy. Analysis of human colon cancer liver metastases single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) datasets revealed that histone methyltransferases of histone 3 lysine 9 trimethylation (H3K9me3) are upregulated in colon tumors and expressed in subsets of T cells in liver metastases of patients with human colon cancer. Targeted therapy with the H3K9me3-specific histone methyltransferase inhibitor F5446 suppresses colon tumor liver metastasis. scRNA-seq analysis revealed the accumulation of PD-1+Tim3+ exhausted T (Tex) cells in mouse colon tumor liver metastases, and F5446 treatment increased the level of IFNγhighPD-1low Tex cells. Furthermore, F5446 therapy increased IFNγhigh intermediate Tex (Tex-int) cells in human colon cancer patient liver metastases-derived xenografts (PDX) and suppressed PDX growth in humanized mice. In patients with human colon cancer, response to pembrolizumab is associated with tumor-infiltrating IFNγhigh Tex cells. Our findings determine that H3K9me3 promotes differentiation of Tex cells and targeting H3K9me3 is an effective approach to increase IFNγhigh Tex-int cells to reinvigorate CTL functionality to suppress colon cancer liver metastasis.

papers.title: CD266+ Myofibroblasts Mediate Resistance to Immunochemotherapy through ECM Stiffness in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
papers.authors: Ju H, Lu Y, Shi C, Zheng Z, Bi Y, Yang W, Guo Z, Dashti MD, Yan M, Ren G, Hu J.
papers.abstract: The efficacy of immunotherapy in unresectable/recurrent/metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (U/R/M HNSCC) remains suboptimal compared with primary untreated resectable HNSCC. The immunologic and stromal landscape during immunotherapy in U/R/M HNSCC is crucial for understanding drug resistance mechanisms. In this study, single-cell RNA sequencing was performed on 42 pre- and posttreatment samples from patients in our prospective trial (NCT05156970) who received immunochemotherapy. A subset of myofibroblasts expressing CD266 was identified as hampering the response to immunochemotherapy in patients with U/R/M HNSCC. This distinct subtype of cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAF) enhanced extracellular matrix (ECM) stiffness and cellular tension through a PIEZO1-mediated biomechanical mechanism, spatially segregated CD8+ T-cell infiltration to establish immune-excluded niches, and ultimately facilitated immune evasion. Mechanistically, PIEZO1 inhibition suppressed YAP activation and reduced FAK phosphorylation, thereby mitigating matrix remodeling effects driven by myofibroblastic CAF CD266. We also observed that PIEZO1 inhibition had a synergistic effect with PD-1 blockade in HNSCC in vivo. In summary, our findings reveal an immunosuppressive mechanism in which stromal cells regulate ECM stiffness, presenting a potential therapeutic target for U/R/M HNSCC.

papers.title: Quantification of Anti-Ro52, Anti-Ro60 and Anti-La Autoantibodies at High Sample Dilution and Their Predictive Value for Congenital Heart Block.
papers.authors: Rudolph L, Möller ER, Rodrigues RDS, de Fremont GM, Ottosson V, Lagnefeld L, Gunnarsson I, Svenungsson E, Nordenstam F, Bergman G, Sonesson SE, Thorlacius GE, Wahren-Herlenius M.
papers.abstract: Maternal anti-Ro/La antibodies confer a risk of congenital heart block (CHB), but current methods for predicting risk relying on the presence or absence of these autoantibodies perform poorly. To identify more accurate biomarkers of CHB risk, we investigated the association between maternal levels of autoantibodies and the risk of CHB. A total of 318 women positive for anti-Ro/SSA autoantibodies were included. Autoantibody presence was obtained from health records for all, and ELISA was used to quantify levels of anti-Ro52, anti-Ro60, and anti-La in a subset of 116 women with samples obtained during pregnancy, including 27 CHB-affected pregnancies. Predictive models for CHB risk were developed using logistic regression and machine learning. Anti-Ro/SSA positive women with anti-Ro60 were more likely to have pregnancies with CHB (p < 0.05). Levels of both anti-Ro60 (p < 0.001) and anti-Ro52 (p < 0.05) were significantly higher in CHB-affected pregnancies and correlated (r = 0.8, p < 0.0001), while levels of anti-La did not differ between groups. Levels of anti-Ro60 were identified as the strongest individual predictor of CHB, with a relative risk of 16.3 (95% CI 1.04-255.0, p < 0.001) for the top versus the bottom decile. In all tested combinations, models that included anti-Ro60 levels outperformed models that did not. Models based on anti-Ro60 levels alone reached an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.76 and an odds ratio (OR) per standard deviation increase of 2.8 (95% CI 1.6-5.3). These findings confirm a strong association between maternal anti-Ro antibody levels and CHB risk in anti-SSA-positive pregnancy, highlighting anti-Ro60 autoantibody levels as a valuable biomarker in risk stratification.

papers.title: Transcriptomic Profiling of Mouse Mammary Tumors Enables Prognostic and Predictive Biomarker Discovery for Human Breast Cancer.
papers.authors: Sutcliffe MD, Mott KR, Yilmaz-Swenson T, Felsheim BM, Lobanov AV, Michmerhuizen AR, Rädler PD, Okumu DO, He X, Pfefferle AD, Dance-Barnes S, Brueffer C, Saal LH, East MP, Hollern DP, Elston TC, Johnson GL, Perou CM.
papers.abstract: The development and validation of prognostic and predictive biomarkers in breast cancer are limited by the availability of well-annotated datasets linking tumor molecular features to treatment response and survival outcomes. To address this need, we generated an extensive mouse model dataset comprised of 26 immunocompetent mammary tumor models spanning diverse genetic backgrounds, epithelial-mesenchymal states, the basal-luminal axis, and distinct immune microenvironments. For each model, survival was measured under no treatment, immune checkpoint inhibition (ICI), and carboplatin/paclitaxel chemotherapy, and RNA sequencing was performed on baseline tumors and on 7-day on-treatment samples for both regimens. Baseline murine tumor gene expression features were used to train a machine learning elastic net model that predicted survival outcomes on multiple human breast cancer datasets with performance comparable with that of existing prognostic assays. Models trained for ICI benefit, using either the untreated or 7-day ICI-treated samples, predicted ICI benefit on human ICI-treated datasets, with the 7-day treated tumor model showing better performance. A predictor of carboplatin/paclitaxel response developed from the murine mammary tumor data performed well in mice but did not generalize to human chemotherapy cohorts. Finally, comparison of multiple computational approaches, including XGBoost, random forests, and support vector regression, showed that all methods successfully predicted survival outcomes, with elastic net offering the best performance and interpretability. These results indicate conserved cancer biology between mouse and human tumors for prognosis and ICI response and establish a large preclinical dataset with linked phenotypic and genomic data as a resource for biomarker discovery. Significance The development of a genomically and phenotypically diverse murine tumor dataset with linked treatment outcomes establishes a robust translational resource to develop, test, and benchmark clinically relevant prognostic and therapeutic response biomarkers.

papers.title: Integrated Transcriptomic and Single-Cell RNA Sequencing Analyses Identify Shared Inflammation-Related Candidate Genes in Psoriasis and Acute Myocardial Infarction.
papers.authors: Fang RN, Shen Y, Li JH, Zhu BC, Jia N, Chen Y, Feng HS, Zhang WT.
papers.abstract: Background Psoriasis and acute myocardial infarction (AMI) are both closely associated with immune-inflammatory dysregulation; however, the shared molecular features of psoriasis-AMI comorbidity remain incompletely characterized. To address this gap, this study aimed to identify novel shared inflammation-related candidate genes between psoriasis and AMI and to characterize their cellular expression patterns using public transcriptomic and single-cell RNA sequencing data. The main finding was the identification of shared inflammation-related candidate genes and their cell-type-specific expression patterns in psoriasis-AMI comorbidity. Methods Transcriptomic datasets related to psoriasis and AMI were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database. GSE30999 and GSE66360 were used as discovery cohorts. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified using limma with adjusted P value Results A total of 57 shared DEGs were identified in the psoriasis and AMI discovery cohorts, including 51 commonly upregulated and 6 commonly downregulated genes. Enrichment analysis showed that these genes were mainly involved in processes related to cellular response to lipopolysaccharide, chemotaxis, cytokine activity and chemokine activity, and were significantly enriched in the IL-17, NF-κB, TNF and chemokine signaling pathways, as well as lipid and atherosclerosis-related pathways. PPI network and cytoHubba analyses identified 9 consensus hub genes. External validation and ROC analyses showed that S100A9, S100A12 and CXCL1 were significantly upregulated in both psoriasis and AMI validation datasets and showed moderate discriminatory performance between groups. Single-cell analysis showed that S100A9 and S100A12 exhibited prominent myeloid inflammation-related expression profiles in psoriatic lesions and AMI peripheral immune cells, whereas CXCL1 expression was relatively restricted, suggesting that it may primarily reflect chemokine-mediated inflammatory cell recruitment. Conclusion This study identified S100A9, S100A12 and CXCL1 as candidate genes potentially associated with shared inflammatory features of psoriasis-AMI comorbidity. These findings suggest that myeloid cell activation and chemokine-mediated recruitment of inflammatory cells may contribute to the molecular link between the two diseases; however, further clinical and experimental validation is required.

papers.title: Identification of Five Candidate Genes and Development of an Exploratory Diagnostic Nomogram for COPD Using Integrative Single-Cell and Bulk Transcriptomic Analyses.
papers.authors: Wang J, Zhang H, Mu Q, Li X, Sun D.
papers.abstract: Background Integrative transcriptomic analyses can prioritize genes associated with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), but expression associations require experimental assessment. Methods Single-cell GSE173896 and bulk GSE57148 data were analyzed using clustering, co-expression networks, CellChat, differential expression, immune deconvolution, pseudotime, and virtual knockout analysis. A five-gene logistic nomogram was developed in GSE57148. Clinical RT-qPCR included 30 participants with COPD and 30 without COPD. Two independent IL6-targeting siRNAs were examined in HBEC3-KT and BEAS-2B cells using epithelial-macrophage co-culture, cytokine measurements, and wound-healing assays. Results NHSL2, CDKL5, CRIP1, TNNI2, and IL6 were prioritized as candidate genes. Clinical RT-qPCR supported higher CDKL5, IL6, and NHSL2 expression and lower CRIP1 and TNNI2 expression in COPD. IL6 knockdown reduced epithelial IL6 expression and attenuated several macrophage-associated transcriptional responses in co-culture after epithelial cigarette smoke extract exposure. Secretory responses varied by cell line and siRNA; co-culture IL-10 reductions were significant in the HBEC3-KT system but not in the BEAS-2B system. IL6 knockdown also reduced epithelial wound closure. The nomogram was evaluated within its development cohort and lacked independent external validation. Conclusion The study identifies five COPD-associated candidate genes and provides experimental evidence linking epithelial IL6 perturbation to selected co-culture responses and wound closure. These findings do not establish a COPD-specific mechanism or therapeutic benefit. The nomogram remains exploratory and requires independent validation.
papers.venue: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease

papers.title: Mechanism Study of Ginsenoside Rd in the Prevention and Treatment of Post-Myocardial Infarction Heart Failure: Network Pharmacology Combined with in vivo and in vitro Experiments Verification.
papers.authors: Zhao T, Liao H, Wang R, Xiao B, Li Z, Qu F, Lu M, Yang Z, Ni S, Wang X.
papers.abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the immunoprotective mechanisms of GSRd, an active ingredient of Panax ginseng C.A. Mey ( P. ginseng C.A. Mey), against post-MI HF, with particular focus on its regulatory effects on regulatory T cells (Tregs) and Monocytes/macrophages (Mos/Mφs). Materials and methods UPLC-MS/MS was used to identify GSRd. A mouse post-MI HF model was established by LAD ligation to observe GSRd-mediated changes in Tregs, IL-10 and Mos/Mφs. Network pharmacology predicted GSRd core targets against post-MI HF. Single-cell virtual knockout evaluated target function, while protein-protein docking predicted IL-10-core target binding regions. In vitro, LPS-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages were applied for inflammatory modeling, with exogenous IL-10 as positive control and Stattic for functional reverse validation of GSRd. Results UPLC-MS/MS confirmed GSRd in P. ginseng C.A. Mey. GSRd ameliorated cardiac function and alleviated myocardial fibrosis in post-MI HF mice. Immunologically, GSRd facilitated the recruitment of Tregs in failing myocardium and peripheral circulation and elevated IL-10 expression. Furthermore, GSRd promoted the polarization of Mos/Mφs toward anti-inflammatory Ly6C low phenotype (with upregulated CD206 and Arg1), suppressed pro-inflammatory Ly6C high polarization, and reduced the secretion of TNF-ppressed pro-inflammatory Ly6Cin post-MI HF mice. Immunologically, GSRd facilitated the recruitment of Tregs in failing myocardium and peripheral ci of STAT3 in cardiac monocytes/macrophages predicted that STAT3 acts as a critical regulator maintaining cardiac inflammatory balance and immune homeostasis. Protein-protein interaction analysis predicted the binding domains between IL-10 and STAT3; molecular docking predicted that ginsenoside Rd can stably bind to Foxp3, IL-10 and STAT3. In vitro experiments revealed that GSRd promotes STAT3 phosphorylation to induce RAW264.7 macrophage polarization toward an anti-inflammatory phenotype, and Stattic attenuates the protective effects of GSRd. Conclusion The present study demonstrates that GSRd confers therapeutic benefits against post-MI HF via modulating the cardiac immune microenvironment.

papers.title: Pharmacologically programmed tolerogenic dendritic cell membrane-coated nanoparticles for CCR7-dependent lymphoid organ targeting in transplantation.
papers.authors: Wu Z, Zhou K, Wang N, Yan J, Lu Z, Fu Y, Tong X, Xiang Y, Shi Y, Yang S, Su R, Guo D, Yu L, Sun R, Tang H, Han W.
papers.abstract: Secondary lymphoid organs (SLOs) are critical sites for alloimmune activation and attractive targets for transplantation immunotherapy. However, current cell membrane-based targeting strategies face a fundamental trade-off between low immunogenicity and efficient SLO homing, limiting their therapeutic potential. To resolve this functional trade-off, we developed a biomimetic delivery system (PD-DmRK) by coating self-assembled RapaLink-1 (RK) nanoparticles with cell membranes derived from PP242 and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA)-induced tolerogenic dendritic cells (TolDCs). Compared with conventional tolerogenic induction strategies, PP242/DHA preserved low immunogenicity and markedly increased CCR7 expression, thereby improving SLO targeting. Mechanistically, PP242 and DHA cooperatively activated the transcription factor USF2, which directly bound to the Ccr7 promoter and transcriptionally upregulated Ccr7 expression. Consequently, PD-DmRK exhibited enhanced accumulation in SLOs, reduced hepatic and renal sequestration, and significantly prolonged skin and cardiac allograft survival. High-dimensional spectral flow cytometry and single-cell transcriptomic analyses further indicated that PD-DmRK treatment was associated with enrichment of Ccr9-expressing plasmacytoid dendritic cells and regulatory T cells, accompanied by reduced cytotoxic T-cell responses. Overall, PD-DmRK provides a TolDC membrane platform in which the USF2-CCR7 axis links immunoregulatory activity with CCR7-dependent SLO targeting, supporting its potential for targeted immunotherapy in transplantation.

papers.title: Integrated Single-cell and Bulk Transcriptomic Analysis Links NOTCH Signaling to Stromal Features and Prognosis in Gastric Cancer.
papers.authors: Jin M, Cui Z, Zhang J, Mi J, Lu S, Zhang X.
papers.abstract: Introduction NOTCH signaling is frequently dysregulated in Gastric Cancer (GC) and has been implicated in stromal and immune regulation. This study aimed to characterize NOTCH-associated intercellular communication and develop a transcriptome-based risk model for survival stratification and exploratory prediction of treatment response. Methods The Seurat package was used to process scRNA-seq data. CellChat was applied to infer intercellular communication networks, with a focus on NOTCH-associated crosstalk. In the TCGA-STAD cohort, we calculated a NOTCH pathway activity score and used WGCNA to identify the module most strongly correlated with that score. Univariate Cox, LASSO Cox, and multivariate Cox regression were then used to derive a five-gene Riskscore. A separate multivariable Cox model evaluated its association with Overall Survival (OS) after adjustment for age, sex, AJCC stage, and histological grade. Prognostic performance was assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and time-dependent ROC curves and was externally evaluated in GSE66229. Immune and stromal features were quantified using ssGSEA, MCPcounter, and ESTIMATE. TIDE and pRRophetic were used for in silico estimates of immunotherapy response and drug sensitivity, respectively. Results Single-cell analysis showed shifts in the relative cellular composition of GC samples, including higher proportions of T cells and macrophages/monocytes and a lower proportion of B cells. CellChat inferred broader NOTCH-associated communication in tumor samples, particularly between fibroblasts and endothelial cells. WGCNA identified a green-yellow module that was most strongly correlated with the NOTCH activity score and was enriched in extracellular matrix organization. A five-gene module-derived Riskscore stratified OS in TCGA-STAD and GSE66229, although time-dependent discrimination varied across cohorts and follow-up intervals. In the complete-case TCGA-STAD analysis, the Riskscore remained associated with OS after adjustment for age, sex, AJCC stage, and histological grade (HR per SD = 1.28, 95% CI: 1.07-1.53, p = 0.007). High-risk tumors had higher immune and stromal scores and higher expression of CD80, CTLA4, and HAVCR2. TIDE and drug-sensitivity estimates suggested subgroup differences; these results remain hypothesis-generating because they were not validated experimentally. Discussion This integrative computational study identified associations among NOTCH pathway activity, inferred fibroblast-endothelial communication, extracellular-matrix programs, and a five-gene prognostic score. The five genes are not canonical NOTCH components; rather, they were selected from a co-expression module correlated with the NOTCH activity score. The findings therefore support an indirect, data-driven association and do not establish that NOTCH signaling causes stromal remodeling, immune evasion, or drug response. Conclusion NOTCH pathway activity was associated with stromal and immune features in GC, and a five-gene module-derived Riskscore provided prognostic stratification with variable discrimination across cohorts. Independent single-cell and experimental validation is required before the inferred crosstalk or treatment-response estimates can inform clinical decisions.

papers.title: Microenvironment-Dependent Role of PLOD3 in Glioblastoma: Associations with Matrix Remodeling and Myeloid Immune Remodeling.
papers.authors: Luo W, Xu X, Zhou L, Gu S, Wang W, Fang J, Peng X, He J, Huang K, Sun D, Yu W, Yin Y.
papers.abstract: Introduction/objective Glioblastoma progression depends on reciprocal interactions between malignant cells, extracellular matrix remodeling, and myeloid immune suppression. However, whether PLOD3 drives glioblastoma through tumor cell-intrinsic or microenvironment- dependent mechanisms remains unclear. Methods This retrospective multi-cohort observational study integrated transcriptomic datasets (GSE68848 and GSE16011), single-cell RNA sequencing reanalysis, immunohistochemistry of 70 glioma specimens, and functional validation in the GL261 murine model using in vitro assays and a subcutaneous syngeneic tumor model. Results PLOD3 was significantly upregulated in glioblastoma and was associated with higher tumor grade, IDH1-wild-type status, and shorter overall survival. Higher PLOD3 expression was associated with increased macrophage infiltration, whereas computational immune-infiltration analyses indicated reduced CD8+ T-cell and natural killer (NK)-cell signatures. PLOD3 knockdown did not appreciably alter GL261 cell proliferation in vitro but significantly reduced subcutaneous tumor growth in immunocompetent mice, accompanied by decreased macrophage infiltration and collagen deposition. Discussion These findings support a microenvironment-dependent role for PLOD3 in the GL261 model rather than a major cell-intrinsic effect on tumor-cell proliferation. Extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling and cytokine-associated signaling identified by transcriptomic analysis represent candidate mechanisms that may contribute to macrophage-dominant microenvironmental remodeling, but these pathways were not directly validated. Conclusion PLOD3 is upregulated in glioblastoma and is associated with poor prognosis and a macrophage-enriched tumor microenvironment. PLOD3 knockdown suppresses tumor growth in vivo and reduces macrophage infiltration and collagen deposition. These findings support a microenvironment-dependent role of PLOD3 in glioblastoma progression, while ECM remodeling and cytokine-associated signaling may contribute to this effect and require further mechanistic validation.

papers.title: Real-world clinical effectiveness and exploratory longitudinal immunological changes of Efgartigimod in myasthenia gravis: a retrospective study and a single-cell analysis in one patient.
papers.authors: Tian L, Zhang L, Jin J, Wang X, Chen Z, Qiao L, Guo Q, Li Y, Zhang J, Zhao Y, Wang L, Li L, Wang J.
papers.abstract: Introduction Efgartigimod, an antagonist of the neonatal Fc receptor, has demonstrated efficacy in generalized myasthenia gravis, but evidence from routine clinical practice remains limited, and its immunological effects beyond immunoglobulin G reduction are incompletely understood. Methods We retrospectively evaluated the 12-week effectiveness and safety of Efgartigimod in 21 patients with acetylcholine receptor antibody-positive generalized myasthenia gravis. Outcomes included changes in Myasthenia Gravis Activities of Daily Living scores, response rates defined by reductions of ≥2 and ≥5 points, achievement of minimal symptom expression, changes in prednisone dosage, and adverse events. To explore potential longer-term immune changes, paired peripheral blood mononuclear cell samples obtained from one patient at baseline and after 6 months of repeated treatment were analyzed using single-cell RNA sequencing and T- and B-cell receptor repertoire sequencing. Results The median MG-ADL score decreased from 7.0 (IQR, 6.0-8.0) at baseline to 1.0 (IQR, 1.0-1.5) at week 12. After the first and second treatment cycles, 85.7 and 94.7% of patients achieved CMI, respectively, while 57.1 and 84.2% achieved ≥5-point reductions. At week 12, 73.7% of patients achieved MSE. Treatment was generally well tolerated, with two mild adverse events and no serious adverse events. Exploratory longitudinal profiling in one patient identified reduced myeloid inflammatory activity and antigen-presentation signatures, attenuated predicted inflammatory intercellular communication, and a more dispersed pattern of T- and B-cell clonal expansion after prolonged treatment. Conclusion The clinical cohort findings support the effectiveness and favorable safety profile of Efgartigimod in routine practice. The exploratory single-cell and immune repertoire analyses from one patient provide preliminary insights into potential immunological changes beyond IgG reduction and require validation in larger cohorts.

papers.title: Lymphocyte trajectories after liver transplantation: immune mechanisms, clinical associations, and research priorities.
papers.authors: Gao J, Shi Z, Jin X, Jiao Z, Xu Z, Ye G, Wang Y, Guo F, Yang L, Gao Z.
papers.abstract: Liver transplantation (LT) is an established treatment for end-stage liver disease, yet rejection, infection, biliary injury, post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder, and tumour recurrence continue to limit outcomes. Post-transplant immune states reflect alloantigen exposure, immunosuppression, microbial or viral stimulation, and inflammation within the graft. This Review examines longitudinal changes in CD8 + and CD4 + T cells, regulatory and follicular T-cell populations, B cells, natural killer cells, mucosal-associated invariant T cells, and γδ T cells after LT. The most direct evidence concerns acute cellular rejection, in which transient effector activation, T helper 1/interferon-γ responses, multicellular T-cell-B-cell signatures, and graft-local clonal programmes have been described. Early infection has been linked to inhibitory-receptor coexpression and impaired protective function, although treatment exposure, viral history, and phenotype definitions affect interpretation. An increase in circulating regulatory T cells alone does not establish operational tolerance; donor specificity, suppressive stability, and intrahepatic localisation are also required. Evidence relating lymphocyte subsets to biliary, vascular, metabolic, and oncological outcomes is less direct and often comes from experimental or non-transplant studies. Meaningful interpretation requires attention to sampling time, anatomical compartment, cellular function, and treatment exposure. Serial blood phenotyping may be combined with functional assays, soluble immune-mediator or protein signatures, graft histology, immune-receptor repertoires, and selected single-cell or spatial analyses. This approach defines research priorities, not a validated score or treatment algorithm. Clinical use will require standardised sampling, prespecified outcomes, externally validated thresholds, and prospective strategy trials that assess both benefit and harm.

papers.title: T cells in type 1 diabetes: mechanisms of β-cell autoimmunity, innate-adaptive immune crosstalk, and translational immunotherapy.
papers.authors: Amer B, Alnukhali M, Haidarah A, Ahmad A.
papers.abstract: Type 1 diabetes (T1D) is an autoimmune disease in which immune responses drive the destruction of insulin-producing pancreatic β-cells, ultimately resulting in lifelong insulin dependence. Although T cells are central mediators of β-cell autoimmunity, growing evidence shows that innate immune cells, including dendritic cells, macrophages, and natural killer (NK) cells, play essential roles in initiating, shaping, and sustaining pathogenic adaptive responses within the islet microenvironment. Both CD4 + helper and CD8 + cytotoxic T lymphocytes contribute to β-cell injury through the production of inflammatory cytokines, direct cytotoxicity, and disruption of self-tolerance. At the same time, regulatory T cells exhibit reduced numbers and/or impaired suppressive function, thereby further accelerating autoimmune progression. Recent advances in animal models, single-cell transcriptomics, spatial immune profiling, and T cell receptor sequencing have refined our understanding of autoreactive repertoires, antigen specificity, and bidirectional crosstalk between innate and adaptive immune compartments. At the translational level, immune signatures are emerging as tools for disease prediction and patient stratification, while therapeutic strategies ranging from anti-CD3 monoclonal antibodies to tolerogenic vaccines and adoptive Treg therapies are moving from preclinical development into clinical evaluation. The clinical success of teplizumab as the first disease-modifying therapy for T1D reinforces the value of targeting immune pathways, but durable remission across diverse patient groups remains a major challenge. This review synthesizes recent advances in the immunobiology of T cells in T1D, emphasizing their functional interplay with innate immune cells, tracing the path from mechanistic discovery to clinical translation, and highlighting future directions for precision immunotherapy.

papers.title: Single-cell transcriptome sequencing analysis of peripheral blood mononuclear cells reveals immune signatures in patients with polymyalgia rheumatica.
papers.authors: Cai T, Qin Q, Jiang Y, Liu Z, Song R, Zhang JA.
papers.abstract: Background Polymyalgia rheumatica (PMR) is an auto-inflammatory disease or autoimmune disease that involves multiple immune cells. In this study, single-cell transcriptome sequencing (scRNA-seq) combined with cellular communication analysis were used to investigate immune characteristics of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) in PMR patients. Methods Three newly diagnosed PMR patients were recruited; their PBMCs were isolated and sequenced on the Illumina NovaSeq 6000 sequencing platform. The PBMCs scRNA-seq data of three normal controls were downloaded from the 10× Genomics platform for joint analysis. Results Relative to healthy controls, PMR patients exhibited a reduced abundance of circulating T cells, alongside an expanded megakaryocyte/platelet compartment. At the T cell subset level, PMR was associated with an increased proportion of pro-inflammatory KIR + NK-like T cells, while CD4 + central memory T cells, effector memory T cells, and Th1 cells showed reductions in relative abundance. Circulating NK cell subsets were disproportionately represented in PMR patients; notably, the CD56 dim CD16 hi -ISG subset was exclusively detected in PMR cases. While no statistically meaningful shifts were observed in the global proportional distribution of B cells, the unswitched memory B cell compartment was absent in PMR patients. Multiple monocyte subsets annotated for elevated inflammatory and interferon-stimulated gene signatures, including CD14_Monocyte-ISG and CD16_Monocyte-IFITM1, were uniformly expanded in the PMR cohort. Functional enrichment analysis showed that the co-stimulation, cytotoxicity, antigen processing and presentation, and inflammation promotion of various immune cells in PMR patients were all enhanced. Key inflammatory pathways were widely activated, including the interferon-γ signaling pathway, interleukin-1β production, and NK cell-mediated cytotoxicity. Cellular communication analysis revealed more interactions but slightly weaker strength in PMRs, with increased communication in TGF-β and CD48 pathways. Conclusions This preliminary study may help to further elucidate the pathogenesis of PMR and provide a theoretical basis for identifying diagnostic markers and discovering new therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Single-cell transcriptome analysis of muscle and blood tissues from a patient with a rare homozygous ANO5 variant causing limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type R12.
papers.authors: Chen M, Dong G, Wang Y, Liu J, Wang Z, Bao D, Huang Z, Li X, Li Y, Cai Z, Wei W.
papers.abstract: Background Limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type R12 (LGMD R12) is a recessive genetic myopathy, typically caused by pathogenic variants in anoctamin-5 (ANO5) , which encodes a multipass membrane protein localized to the sarcolemma and sarcoplasmic reticulum of muscle fibers. Effective therapeutic strategies for LGMD R12 remain elusive. A comprehensive analytical framework is required to dissect the cellular and molecular changes underlying this disease. Methods The ANO5 variant in the patient and his family members was validated by Sanger sequencing. We performed single-cell RNA sequencing analysis on biceps brachii muscle tissue (MUS) and peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from healthy controls (HCs) and a patient who was homozygous for the pathogenic variant in exon 10 of ANO5 (c.898dupA, p.Ile300fs). Immunofluorescence staining was conducted to validate key findings from the single-cell transcriptome analysis. Results In the MUS cell atlas , we observed a significant loss of type I muscle fibers in the patient with LGMD R12. Accordingly, immunofluorescence staining revealed a dramatic loss of MYH7 + cells (MYH7 + , a marker of type I muscle fibers) compared with those in controls. Glycolytic pathway activity and cellular metabolic activity were significantly downregulated, suggesting that they are two transcriptomic signatures in the muscle tissue of this patient. In addition, muscle progenitor cells from the patient exhibited impaired differentiation capacity, failing to generate mature myocytes. In both MUS and PBMCs, we also observed heightened immune crosstalk accompanied by significant activation of pathways such as LGALS9-CD45/CD44 and ANXA1-FPR1, suggesting immunological activation in this patient. Conclusion LGMD R12 with pathogenic ANO5 variants is a rare genetic disease. Our transcriptome and experimental analyses revealed dramatic cellular and molecular changes in affected tissue at the single-cell resolution in a patient with LGMD R12. This study provides valuable insights into the underlying mechanisms and potential development of interventions for this recessive genetic myopathy.

papers.title: Longitudinal immune trajectories following SARS-CoV-2 vaccination in long-term care facility residents: an unsupervised analysis approach.
papers.authors: Palmieri A, Damiano C, Leone P, Trevisan C, Malara A, Zucchelli A, Incalzi RA, Prato R, Fortunato F, Baldovin T, Coin A, Minchella P, Giordano S, Palamara AT, Onder G, Fedele G.
papers.abstract: Background Residents of Long-Term Care Facilities (LTCFs) represent a highly vulnerable population characterized by immunosenescence, multimorbidity, and heterogeneous immune responses to repeated SARS-CoV-2 vaccination and infection. Conventional analyses based on single clinical variables often fail to capture this complexity. We evaluated longitudinal humoral immune responses in institutionalized older adults to identify data-driven antibody profiles and characterize cluster-specific waning kinetics. Methods In a prospective multicenter cohort of 388 Italian LTCF residents followed across four time points (T0-T3 over 12 months), longitudinal anti-Spike (anti-S) and anti-Nucleocapsid (anti-N) IgG levels were measured alongside demographic and vaccination data. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) was used for dimensionality reduction, followed by K-means clustering. Optimal cluster number was determined using internal validation metrics (Silhouette, Calinski-Harabasz, and Davies-Bouldin indices) and bootstrap stability analysis. Linear mixed-effects models were applied to describe cluster-specific antibody waning trajectories. Results A longitudinal analysis was conducted on 388 LTCF residents. Three antibody trajectory profiles emerged: (i) a Vaccine-Driven profile (n = 130), characterized by moderate anti-S titers and progressive antibody decline; (ii) a Hybrid Immunity profile (n = 125), characterized by evidence of prior infection and remarkably stable antibody concentrations throughout follow-up despite limited uptake of the 2023/2024 booster; and (iii) a High-Peak Hybrid Responder profile (n = 133), exhibiting the highest baseline anti-S titers followed by the steepest rate of antibody waning. Across the cohort, 12 of 388 residents (3.1%) developed documented symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection during follow-up, with no COVID-19-related deaths and no significant difference in infection incidence among profiles. Bootstrap stability analysis showed a mean Adjusted Rand Index (ARI) of 0.74 (SD 0.20). Conclusion Unsupervised machine learning effectively resolves the complex heterogeneity of SARS-CoV-2 humoral responses in LTCF residents into data-driven trajectory patterns. These findings illustrate the utility of data-driven approach for describing humoral dynamics while distinguishing observational antibody kinetics from direct estimates of clinical protection.

papers.title: Molecular endotyping in systemic lupus erythematosus: an integrative framework toward precision therapy.
papers.authors: Terajima Y, Matsumoto Y, Nawachi S, Asano Y, Hayashi K, Miyawaki Y, Watanabe H, Katsuyama E, Katsuyama T, Wada J.
papers.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a clinically defined syndrome arising from heterogeneous and dynamically interacting molecular programs. Recent transcriptomic, single-cell, spatial, and functional studies have identified recurrent molecular states; however, published three-, five-, six-, and eight-group taxonomies are not directly interchangeable. In this review, the published evidence was synthesized within a pragmatic framework of four overlapping candidate programs: interferon/interferon-stimulated gene (IFN/ISG), B cell/plasmablast, neutrophil/neutrophil extracellular trap (NET), and an emerging immunometabolic program. Complement/immune-complex activation is considered a cross-cutting effector axis rather than a mutually exclusive endotype. The molecular endotype is defined operationally, and a distinction is made between pathway signatures, candidate endotypes, and clinically actionable endotypes. In this review, activity biomarkers, prognostic biomarkers, pharmacodynamic biomarkers, and predictive biomarkers are distinguished; the transcriptomic ISG-high states are distinguished from directly measurable type I IFN bioactivity; and the contributions of short-lived plasmablasts and long-lived plasma cells to autoantibody production are also examined. It should be emphasized that endotype assignment is time- and compartment-dependent and that blood signatures may not fully capture organ-specific disease, particularly lupus nephritis. Molecular endotyping in SLE should therefore be viewed as a research framework toward precision therapy rather than as a current treatment algorithm. Prospective biomarker-enriched trials and longitudinal multi-compartment profiling will be required to establish clinically actionable endotypes.

papers.title: MZT1 as a Prognostic and Immune-related Biomarker Promoting Invasion and Metastasis in Lung Adenocarcinoma.
papers.authors: Hu Z, Chen Y, Chen Y, Fu J, Wang Y.
papers.abstract: Introduction Our preliminary findings indicate that bioinformatic analysis of the Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) database reveals a significant upregulation of Mitotic-Spindle Organizing Protein 1 (MZT1) in Lung Adenocarcinoma (LUAD) cohorts compared to normal controls; however, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain elusive. To investigate the expression of MZT1 in LUAD cells, its role in tumor invasion and metastasis, and its potential as a biomarker for LUAD. Methods The differential expression of MZT1 at both mRNA and protein levels between LUAD tissues and adjacent normal tissues was analyzed using the TCGA, TIMER, and UALCAN databases. Differentially expressed genes between high- and low-MZT1 expression groups were screened using R packages and Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA), followed by biological pathway enrichment analysis. Quantitative real-time Polymerase Chain Reaction (qPCR) was employed to detect MZT1 expression levels in LUAD cell lines. MZT1-knockdown cell lines were constructed, and functional validation was performed using Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8), colony formation, and Transwell assays. Results Bioinformatics analysis confirmed MZT1 is highly expressed in LUAD tissues, with expression levels varying significantly by patient gender, smoking status, T-stage, and survival duration. Univariate and multivariate Cox regression analyses identified MZT1 as an independent prognostic factor for LUAD, with ROC analysis suggesting a potential diagnostic value within the TCGA cohort (AUC = 0.712). Higher MZT1 expression correlated with poorer Overall Survival (OS) and Disease-Specific Survival (DSS). GO/KEGG and GSEA analyses linked MZT1 to cell cycle regulation, oocyte meiosis, and cell cycle checkpoint signaling. MZT1 expression positively correlated with tumor mutational burden and showed significant associations with reduced immune infiltrates. Cell experiments show that knockdown of MZT1 can inhibit LUAD cell proliferation, colony formation, migration and invasion, as well as the Epithelial-Mesenchymal Transition (EMT) process. Discussion Although MZT1 is recognized as a fundamental component of the γ-Tubulin Ring Complex (γ-TuRC), its role in LUAD remains unexplored. Our bioinformatic and clinical analyses revealed that MZT1 is significantly upregulated in LUAD and is closely associated with advanced clinical stages and poor overall survival, and it serves as an independent prognostic factor with potential diagnostic value. Mechanistically, MZT1 is strongly enriched in cell cycle regulation pathways and correlates negatively with multiple immune infiltrating cells, suggesting it may promote tumor progression and facilitate immune evasion. Notably, the positive correlation between MZT1 expression and TMB, combined with suppressed immune infiltration, highlights a unique immune phenotype characterized by high genomic instability and effective immune exclusion. In vitro experiments demonstrated that MZT1 knockdown significantly inhibits LUAD cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and EMT, indicating its dual role in driving primary tumor growth and metastatic potential. However, this study is limited by the lack of in vivo validation and detailed molecular mechanisms. Future studies utilizing animal models and multi-omics approaches are warranted to elucidate the precise downstream signaling pathways and therapeutic potential of MZT1 in LUAD. Conclusion MZT1 is highly expressed in LUAD tissues and is associated with immune infiltration in tumors. Functional enrichment and in vitro experiments suggest that MZT1 may promote LUAD progres-sion by regulating cell cycle-related pathways and EMT, thereby driving cell proliferation and metastasis.

papers.title: Antibody afucosylation and enhanced autoreactive antibody response are associated with thyroid dysfunction during severe SARS-CoV-2 infection.
papers.authors: Pesce E, Gobbini A, Bombaci M, Favalli A, Maioli S, Serapian SA, di Marzo N, Sorrentino L, Toccafondi M, Gruarin P, Lombardi A, Armenti M, Lorenzo M, Bandera A, Colombo G, Muller I, Grifantini RM.
papers.abstract: Introduction SARS-CoV-2 infections causing severe COVID-19 are known to induce or exacerbate thyroid dysfunctions (TD), comprising autoimmune thyroiditis and subacute thyroiditis. Non-thyroidal illness syndrome is also common. Thyroid damage could result from direct viral infection and/or aberrant immuno-inflammatory responses. However, the specific immunological mechanisms contributing to TD in severe COVID-19 are not fully understood. Methods We investigated the relationship between severe SARS-CoV-2 infection and TD by analyzing antibody autoreactivity and fucosylation level in 40 COVID-19 patients recruited during the 2020 pandemic wave. Using protein arrays, ELISA, and computational modeling, we compared patients with and without TD to 20 healthy controls and 29 Graves' disease cases, focusing on the functional impact of the elicited antibodies. Results We observed a significant shift in IgG autoreactivity, specifically targeting CD16A and KIR2DL1 in COVID-19 patients, both TD and not-TD, compared to Healthy Controls (HC) or other thyroid disease patients. Anti-Spike IgGs from COVID-19-TD patients exhibited a lower fucosylation state compared with those without TD and were associated with increased NK-cell activation and degranulation. Furthermore, patients' sera showed increased binding to immortalized human thyroid epithelial cells. Computational analysis identified structural similarities between the SARS-CoV-2 Spike protein and thyroglobulin. Discussion Thyroid damage in severe COVID-19 involves a complex interplay of different mechanisms. We proposed a potential role of lowly fucosylated anti-Spike antibodies, which may contribute to heightened NK cell-mediated activation via CD16A, potentially exacerbated by virus-induced autoreactivity. Altered IgG fucosylation and autoreactivity are associated with thyroid dysfunctions in severe COVID-19.

papers.title: Cross-cohort blood transcriptome analysis identifies an eight-gene diagnostic index and inflammatory programs in acute myocardial infarction.
papers.authors: Pan C, Chen Z, Li J, Xie S, Fan X.
papers.abstract: Background Globally, acute myocardial infarction (AMI) is the foremost cause of cardiovascular fatality, with dysregulated immune-inflammatory cascades serving as master regulators of both acute cardiomyocyte necrosis and subsequent maladaptive remodeling. Despite the prognostic potential of individual immune biomarkers, no multi-omics machine learning (ML)-derived immune gene signature has been established for predicting AMI outcome. Methods Peripheral blood transcriptomes from four Gene Expression Omnibus datasets (GSE59867 as the discovery cohort; GSE48060, GSE60993, and GSE66360 as independent validation cohorts; total 348 participants) were subjected to study-wise differential expression analysis and marker-based immune scoring without cross-platform batch harmonization. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) and nested machine learning (L2-regularized logistic regression, linear support vector machine (SVM), random forest, and gradient boosting) were used to derive an eight-gene diagnostic index. Signature performance was evaluated in three independent validation cohorts, contextualized at the single-cell resolution (GSE121893), and experimentally supported by in vitro reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) using American Type Culture Collection (ATCC)-authenticated cell lines (THP-1 TIB-202 and EA.hy926 CRL-2922). Results AMI specimens showed marked enrichment of pro-inflammatory M1-like macrophages, neutrophils, and exhausted CD8+ T cells compared to healthy donors. The WGCNA turquoise module exhibited the strongest phenotypic correlation (r = 0.78, p In vitro RT-qPCR in ATCC-authenticated THP-1-derived macrophages (lipopolysaccharide/ATP stimulation) and EA.hy926 cells (hypoxia/reoxygenation) confirmed elevated levels of CXCL10 (3.82 ± 0.31-fold), IL6 (4.15 ± 0.44-fold), NLRP3 (2.94 ± 0.28-fold), and CASP1 (3.47 ± 0.38-fold) under AMI-relevant stimulation conditions ( n = 3 independent biological replicates). Conclusions An eight-gene diagnostic index (BAX, EDA2R, MCEMP1, SOCS3, ASGR2, RNASE1, ADM, and KPNA5), derived using nested machine learning and validated in three independent cohorts, achieved robust discriminative accuracy for AMI diagnosis. Elevated inflammatory transcripts (CXCL10, IL6, NLRP3, and CASP1) confirmed by in vitro RT-qPCR in ATCC cell lines reflect concurrent inflammasome activation and immune dysregulation, offering a mechanistic rationale for precision immune-targeted intervention strategies.

papers.title: Integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses identify key metabolites and genes in sepsis-associated acute lung injury.
papers.authors: Huang H, Zhao L, Chen H, Sui L, Zhu J, Fang X, Li P, Liu H, Wu X, Wang D.
papers.abstract: Introduction Sepsis-associated acute lung injury (SALI) is a life-threatening pulmonary complication of sepsis with high mortality. This study aimed to prioritize serum metabolites and genes potentially involved in SALI by integrating multi-omics datasets. Methods A rat SALI model treated with Xuanbai Chengqi Decoction (XCD) was subjected to untargeted serum metabolomics. Bulk and single-cell RNA-seq datasets were retrieved from GEO, and metabolite-related GWAS statistics were obtained from IEU OpenGWAS. scPagwas mapped metabolite genetic signals to cell populations; hdWGCNA identified cell signature genes. Candidate genes were filtered by overlapping bulk DEGs, ten machine-learning models and expression validation. Functional enrichment, immune infiltration, cell -cell communication, pseudotime and scTenifoldKnk virtual knockdown analyses were performed. Results Oleoylcarnitine showed the strongest genetic association with T cells. Cross-platform integration prioritized GIMAP4 and RCBTB2 as hub genes, with WBP2 retained for further validation. Their expression correlated with altered immune infiltration, especially eosinophils, and the three-gene profiles shared 62 biological processes. SALI exhibited increased number and strength of cell interactions compared with isolated sepsis. Five T-cell subsets were identified, and virtual knockdown of hub genes modified regulation of eight DEGs. Discussion Oleoylcarnitine-associated metabolic changes are correlated with T-cell dysregulation mediated by GIMAP4, RCBTB2, and WBP2 in SALI. These findings are descriptive, and further experiments are required to establish causal relationships.

papers.title: Long COVID shows IL-1 pathway dysregulation without a discrete circulating biomarker signature.
papers.authors: Muñoz-López F, Flores-Santamaría M, Santano R, Trigueros M, Riveira-Muñoz E, Cabrero de Las Heras S, Banaei G, Pradenas E, Trinité B, Marfil S, Gervassi A, Urrea V, Izquierdo-Pujol J, Loste C, Santos JR, Lladós G, Aiello TF, Chamorro A, Jiménez A, Dobaño C, Paredes R, Blanco J, Ballana E, Moncunill G, Mateu L, Nevot M, Massanella M.
papers.abstract: Introduction Long COVID (LC) is characterized by persistent and, often, disabling symptoms, yet its biological basis remains unclear. Multiple mechanisms, including immune dysregulation, endothelial dysfunction, and persistence of SARS-CoV-2 components, have been proposed, although it is unknown whether these define distinct biological subtypes or overlapping processes. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of 312 individuals, including 139 people with LC (PWLC), 99 COVID-19-recovered controls (both groups sampled a median of 8 months after primary SARS-CoV-2 infection), and 74 uninfected controls, from an unvaccinated population, thereby minimizing major sources of biological and epidemiological variability. Circulating immune and endothelial biomarkers and plasma SARS-CoV-2 RNA were assessed, together with serological signatures associated with herpesvirus reactivation and SARS-CoV-2-specific humoral responses. Associations with symptom persistence were analyzed using multivariable models and machine learning approaches. Results Most soluble biomarker differences primarily distinguished previously infected individuals from uninfected controls rather than PWLC from recovered participants. Increased IL-1 receptor antagonist (IL-1RA) levels, together with reduced IL-1β/IL-1RA ratios, were the immune alterations most strongly associated with LC, while P-selectin was the endothelial marker showing a suggestive association with symptom persistence. Plasma SARS-CoV-2 RNA was detected at low and comparable frequencies in PWLC and recovered individuals, while Ct values tended to be lower among RNA-positive PWLC not reaching statistical difference. Epstein-Barr virus serological profiles were characterized by lower latency- and higher reactivation-associated responses in PWLC, whereas SARS-CoV-2-specific antibody levels were comparable between groups. Integrated biomarker profiles discriminated prior infection more effectively than LC status, and expansion to multimodal predictors did not clearly improve discrimination between PWLC and recovered participants. Discussion Overall, LC was associated with overlapping immune, endothelial, and virological alterations rather than discrete biomarker-defined subtypes.

papers.title: RhoA Y42C drives cell plasticity and PD-1-mediated immune evasion of diffuse gastric cancer.
papers.authors: Ko KP, Kim S, Jang J, Seo Y, Zou G, Zhang J, Jun S, Morrow B, Ajani JA, Park RJ, Lo YH, Curran MA, Hyunki K, Park JI.
papers.abstract: Diffuse gastric cancer (DGC) is an aggressive gastric cancer subtype with a poor prognosis. The RHOA Y42C mutation is recurrent in DGC, but its independent oncogenic role is unclear. Next-Generation Sequencing of 431 DGC cases revealed that most RHOA mutations occurred without CDH1 alterations. Using genetically engineered gastric organoids, we show that Rhoa Y42C , along with Kras G12D and Trp53 loss (RKP), induces DGC, independently of Cdh1 loss. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics reveal that RKP tumors exhibit mucinous histopathology and a specific lineage trajectory from Aqp5 + cells to Muc1/Muc4 + cells. RKP tumors create an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment where AREG, transactivated by RhoA Y42C-YAP1, causes T cell exhaustion via PD-1 upregulation. Unlike E-cadherin loss-associated DGC, RKP tumors are highly susceptible to PD-1 blockade. Additionally, the RHOA Y42C mutation correlates with PD-1 upregulation in human DGC samples. These findings redefine the oncogenic role of RhoA Y42C, confirming its sufficiency for DGC development and suggesting PD-1 inhibition as a viable therapeutic option for DGC patients carrying this mutation.

papers.title: A multi-center, single-arm, phase 2 trial of dasatinib in T follicular helper cell lymphomas.
papers.authors: Suma S, Sakata-Yanagimoto M, Suehara Y, Ara T, Goto H, Usuki K, Izutsu K, Yamaguchi M, Fukuhara N, Sakaida E, Ohmachi K, Uehara A, Matsue K, Kimura S, Nagai H, Maruyama D, Nishimoto M, Takeuchi K, Nakamura N, Terauchi T, Fujisawa M, Abe Y, Makishima K, Hattori K, Sakamoto T, Kurita N, Nishikii H, Yoshino F, Yoshida K, Hashimoto Y, Kaneta T, Ogawa S, Keino N, Gosho M, Hosokawa H, Steidl C, Hashimoto K, Chiba S.
papers.abstract: T follicular helper cell lymphomas (TFHL) harbor activating T cell receptor (TCR) signaling mutations and epigenetic alterations, such as TET2 mutations. Here, we conduct a multi-center, single-arm, phase 2 trial of the tyrosine kinase inhibitor dasatinib in patients with relapsed/refractory TFHLs (jRCT2031190079). The primary outcome is the overall response rate (ORR) according to CT-based Lugano criteria 2014. Key secondary endpoints include ORR in RHOA-mutated patients and progression-free/overall survival. The main inclusion criteria consist of TFHL diagnosis and relapse following at least 1 prior chemotherapy regimen. Key exclusion criteria encompass central nervous system involvement, history of other malignancies, and receipt of chemotherapy or radiotherapy within 4 weeks. Nineteen patients are enrolled, with 18 receiving dasatinib and 17 evaluable for efficacy. Median age is 73 years, 50% are female, and angioimmunoblastic T cell lymphoma is the predominant subtype (n = 13). Dasatinib yields a 23.5% ORR, below the prespecified 30% endpoint. Treatment-related adverse events occur in 61.1% of patients (n = 11). Patients harboring TCR signaling mutations, especially those with RHOA p.G17V, achieve a 36.4% ORR, whereas no responses are observed in mutation-negative cases. Exploratory single-cell RNA sequencing reveals interferon-γ/tumor necrosis factor-enriched tumor microenvironments and peripheral expansion of cytotoxic T cell clones in responders. Conversely, early progression correlates with a high TET2 mutation burden in non-malignant immune cells, including CD8 + T cell subsets. While the primary outcome is below the prespecified endpoint, our exploratory findings implicate immune dysfunction involving TET2 mutations in limiting the therapeutic benefit of dasatinib.
